F001.name: Inbound iMessage attachments (photos, PDFs, voice memos)
F001.description: Photos, PDFs and voice memos sent to Happy actually reach the agent; today a message that is only an attachment is dropped without a reply.
F001.how: Set channels.imessage.includeAttachments: true; Basic mode already carries media; default attachment root covers the happy user; inbound caps are 10 MB image, 20 MB audio.
corrections: Catalog JSON 'needs' asks for an attachmentRoots entry and treats mediaMaxMb 16 as the limit for incoming files. media.md:23-25 says the default root pattern already covers every user's Messages folder (configured roots are merged, not replaced) and mediaMaxMb is the outbound cap. The Markdown wording already reflects this.

'Under store:false' covers less than it reads. OpenAI's data-controls page says store only governs application state; abuse-monitoring logs with prompt and response content are still kept up to 30 days by default. Family photos sent to the model fall under that unless the OpenAI organisation has Zero Data Retention.
unverified: That the gateway process under the happy account already has Full Disk Access to the Messages attachments folder comes from the 9 Oct notes and was not re-checked.
Whether OpenClaw treats the per-person custom provider ids exactly like the stock OpenAI provider for image input was not tested live (the config repo does declare image input for both models).

sources.title: iMessage media and attachments
sources.supports: Inbound attachments are off by default and attachment-only messages are dropped before the agent until this key is set to true.

sources.title: Enabling the imsg private API
sources.supports: With SIP left on, imsg still sends and receives text and media, so attachments do not need the Private API.

sources.title: Media understanding
sources.supports: Inbound media understanding has default size limits of 10 MB for images and 20 MB for audio, separate from the outbound media cap.

sources.title: Data controls in the OpenAI platform
sources.supports: OpenAI keeps abuse-monitoring logs, which can include prompt and response content, for up to 30 days by default on all API usage unless Zero Data Retention is approved.

F002.name: Photo and PDF understanding
F002.description: Send a photo of a flyer, label or receipt, or a PDF packet, and Happy reads it and answers questions about it.
F002.how: Images pass natively to gpt-6-sol; attached PDFs arrive as extracted text blocks; the optional pdf tool (group:media) adds page selection via local PDFium, 10 MB and 20 pages by default.
corrections: Catalog JSON 'needs' says view_image is already granted and sets agents.defaults.pdfModel to luna. The minimal profile contains only session_status and gateway (tool-policy.md:36), and pdfModel is an agents.defaults key that is unset by default (pdf.md:124). The Markdown already drops both.
unverified: Reading accuracy on blurry phone photos and scanned image-only PDFs was not measured; pages with under 200 characters of text are rendered to images for the vision model (pdf.md:93).
Whether PDF links, as opposed to attachments, should be readable is left open; the pdf tool rejects remote URLs when it runs sandboxed (pdf.md:68).

sources.title: PDF tool
sources.supports: For providers other than Anthropic and Google the pdf tool extracts text and page images locally with the bundled document-extract plugin (clawpdf, PDFium).

sources.title: Media understanding
sources.supports: When the reply model accepts images, OpenClaw hands it the original image instead of a text summary.

sources.title: Configuration — tool policy
sources.supports: The pdf tool belongs to group:media, so under the minimal profile it must be allowed explicitly and any group deny removes it.

sources.title: GPT-6 Sol model reference (OpenAI API docs)
sources.supports: OpenAI lists text and image as this model's input modalities and text as its only output; audio input is not listed.

F003.name: Voice memos in, transcribed locally
F003.description: A parent sends a voice memo instead of typing; the Mac mini transcribes it locally, echoes the text back and answers. Only the transcript reaches the cloud model.
F003.how: Explicit tools.media.models CLI entry (whisper-cli, capabilities audio, {{AttachmentPath}}) plus echoTranscript; needs brew whisper.cpp, ffmpeg and a GGML model file; OpenClaw converts to WAV itself.
corrections: Markdown pairs a whisper-cpp install with audio.preferredModel: "cli:whisper". The matcher compares that value with cli: plus the entry's exact command string (dist/resolve-KJuMET3H.mjs:148), so for whisper-cpp it must be cli:whisper-cli, or cli: plus the full path used in the entry; cli:whisper only matches the Python whisper CLI.

The Homebrew formula is now named whisper.cpp (formerly whisper-cpp) and its page says GGML model files are not downloaded by default. The 9 Oct note about a model that downloads automatically describes the Python whisper CLI (media-understanding.md:168), not whisper-cli.

ffmpeg is a hard requirement the Markdown leaves out: upstream whisper-cli reads only 16-bit WAV (github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp README), OpenClaw shells out to ffmpeg for that conversion (dist/ffmpeg-exec-VIr-PIWC.mjs:25 prints the brew install hint), and the formula does not pull ffmpeg in.
unverified: The container format of iMessage voice memos, and whether ffmpeg decodes it cleanly, were not tested.
Transcription speed on the M5 Pro and accuracy for Chinese or mixed-language speech were not measured.
Whether the per-person custom provider ids count as OpenAI audio auth in auto-detection is undocumented; the explicit CLI entry sidesteps the question.

sources.title: Audio and voice notes
sources.supports: In auto-detection a configured provider API key is tried before any local speech binary, which is why the local CLI has to be listed explicitly to keep audio on the Mac.

sources.title: OpenClaw media-understanding CLI runner (bundled source)
sources.supports: For whisper-cli the runner first converts any non-WAV attachment to 16 kHz mono WAV with ffmpeg, so ffmpeg must be present on the host.

sources.title: Homebrew Formulae: whisper.cpp
sources.supports: The Homebrew formula (formerly whisper-cpp) installs whisper-cli but ships no model files and does not list ffmpeg as a dependency; both must be added separately.

F004.name: Spoken replies (TTS) and voice round trip
F004.description: On request, or after a voice memo, Happy's reply also arrives as an audio file to tap and play. The phone can already read texts aloud in the car.
F004.how: tts provider tts-local-cli running macOS say (WAV file, offline); tts.auto "inbound" per agent or /tts audio on demand; iMessage gets a plain attachment, not a voice bubble.
corrections: Catalog JSON description says the reply returns 'as an MP3 attachment'. With the free say path the file is WAV (tts/output.md:46, configuration.md:143); MP3 comes only from cloud speech providers. The Markdown already says WAV.
unverified: That the documented say preset writes a valid WAV on macOS 27 without extra data-format flags was not run.
How Messages on iPhone presents a WAV attachment (inline player or plain file) was not tested.
The 1,500-character summarise-or-truncate threshold is documented (tts/commands.md:104) but its effect on long replies here was not tried.

sources.title: Text-to-speech field reference
sources.supports: Auto-TTS has an inbound mode that sends audio only after the user has sent a voice message.

sources.title: Text-to-speech configuration
sources.supports: The documented Local CLI preset runs the macOS say command with a WAV output format and needs no API key.

sources.title: Text-to-speech output and Auto-TTS behavior
sources.supports: A Local CLI provider delivers audio in its configured output format, so the say preset yields WAV rather than MP3.

sources.title: Use CarPlay with your iPhone - Apple Support
sources.supports: With iOS 15 or later Siri can read incoming messages aloud in the car, so the phone already covers hands-free listening to Happy's text replies.

F005.name: Image generation (cards, coloring pages, story pictures)
F005.description: A parent asks for a coloring page or card picture and gets an image back on iMessage; it works, but it drags in a provider route this setup avoids.
F005.how: image_generate with openai/gpt-image-2 needs the bundled openai provider (API key or models.providers.openai); that auth then leads audio and PDF auto-selection unless pinned.
corrections: Catalog JSON 'needs' says 'on the existing key (custom provider id, store:false)'. The image route is the bundled openai plugin (image-and-video.md:12), and the Images endpoint has no application-state storage to disable (OpenAI data-controls table). The Markdown already says this.

Catalog JSON 'needs' puts a per-day cap 'in AGENTS.md or plugin config'. A search of image-generation.md in this run found no per-day or quota setting, so a cap can only be a prompt rule plus the OpenAI project budget.
unverified: Price per image for gpt-image-2 and whether the family's OpenAI project has access to it were not checked.
Whether a parent-requested picture for a child counts as kids' content under the family's never list is a policy call, not a sourced fact.
The reviewers' remark that the ChatGPT app already does this was not sourced.

sources.title: OpenAI image generation
sources.supports: Image generation comes from the bundled openai plugin under the openai/gpt-image-2 model ref with an OpenAI API key or Codex OAuth, not from a custom chat provider id.

sources.title: OpenAI advanced configuration
sources.supports: Direct OpenAI Responses models on the stock openai provider have store forced on, which is the chat route this household deliberately avoids.

sources.title: Audio and voice notes
sources.supports: Once OpenAI provider auth exists it is chosen for transcription ahead of local binaries in auto-detection, so local speech-to-text must be pinned first.

sources.title: Data controls in the OpenAI platform
sources.supports: The Images endpoint keeps no application state, so there is no store switch to turn off, but its abuse-monitoring logs are retained for 30 days by default.

F005.reject_reason: Image generation works, but it needs OpenAI's catalog provider, which changes how voice memos and PDFs are routed and has no storage switch; too many side effects for coloring pages.

F006.name: Happy in the parents' group chat (stateless family-group agent + pinned delivery target)
F006.description: Happy joins a three-way iMessage group with both parents, answers when addressed by name, and that chat becomes the place shared announcements land.
F006.how: groupPolicy allowlist with groupAllowFrom and a groups[chat_id] entry; bindings[] with peer kind group routes it to a stateless family-group agent; mention gating uses the agent name.
corrections: Catalog JSON description includes a 'tell everyone dinner is at 6:30' relay and gives the group agent calendar and list tools. Neither exists on the installed stack; the Markdown already moves the relay to G009 and limits version 1 to weather and search.
unverified: Receiving and replying in a three-person group in Basic mode has not been tried live on this Mac; the docs warn that some multi-person threads arrive flagged as non-group unless the chat id is registered (access-control.md:152-153).
Whether a voice memo in the group can satisfy the mention gate on iMessage is not documented (audio.md:286 defers to channel docs).
The numeric chat id is unknown until the group is created and read with imsg chats.

sources.title: iMessage access control and routing
sources.supports: Group messages must pass a sender allowlist and then a per-chat registry keyed by chat_id before they reach an agent.

sources.title: Agent bindings
sources.supports: A binding can match one specific group conversation and route it to a dedicated agent.

sources.title: steipete/imsg README (GitHub)
sources.supports: Without disabling SIP, imsg can list chats with their ids, watch a chat and send text and files; only rich actions and chat management need the injected helper.

F007.name: Timed reminders over iMessage (one-shot and recurring)
F007.description: "Remind me at 4:30 to pick up the kids" or "every Sunday 7 pm: bins out" becomes a scheduled text to the asker, and reminders can be listed and cancelled.
F007.how:
automations tool (cron alias) allowed on

-main; --at one-shots auto-delete; recurring --cron with --tz; jobs capped with --tools ""; only senders in commands.ownerAllowFrom may use it.
corrections: Catalog JSON 'needs' lists --delete-after-run. One-shot --at jobs already delete themselves after confirmed delivery (how-it-works.md:19). The Markdown already says so.
unverified: Creating a reminder from an iMessage owner turn has not been tried live on this install; managing-jobs.md:81 describes chat creation for Control UI administrators, and the owner-only /loop command is the documented chat shortcut for recurring jobs.
The comparison with Siri and Apple Reminders for one-off personal timers was not sourced.

sources.title: Configuration — tool policy
sources.supports: The scheduler is exposed to agents as the automations tool, with cron kept as an alias, inside group:automation.

sources.title: How automations work
sources.supports: One-shot reminders remove themselves once delivery is confirmed, so no clean-up flag is needed.

sources.title: Automation delivery
sources.supports: A reminder an agent creates from a live chat keeps that chat as its delivery target, so it texts the person who asked.

sources.title: Hardened baselines
sources.supports: Only owner senders may use the scheduling tool from chat, so each parent has to be listed as an owner before they can set reminders.

sources.title: Standing intents
sources.supports: Only channel owners receive the intent tool to create, list or cancel standing intents.

sources.title: TriggerBench: Investigating Prospective Memory for Large Language Models (arXiv 2606.23459)
sources.supports: A 2026 benchmark paper finds language models get much worse at acting on a remembered future trigger as context grows, the reason a structural matcher is used here.

sources.title: Automation schedules
sources.supports: A timezone cannot be combined with a fixed-interval schedule, so fixed local dose times need cron expressions or dated one-shots.

sources.title: User model
sources.supports: Cron sessions do not load MEMORY.md, so each reminder must carry its own text and the refill arithmetic happens in the parent's normal chat.

sources.title: Add and log medications with iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch
sources.supports: Apple's Health app already schedules medication alerts and lets the user log each dose as taken or skipped, so per-dose pings duplicate the phone.

sources.title: Memory overview: memory tools
sources.supports: The intent tool is one of three memory tools provided by the active memory plugin, memory-core by default.

sources.title: Use Reminders on your iPhone, iPad, or iPod touch - Apple Support
sources.supports: The built-in Reminders app can raise a reminder when you message a chosen person and can tie a reminder to a location.

adds: The documented limits of topic-triggered intents (keyword match with no model call, 24-hour cooldown, three fires, 90-day expiry, owner-only tool) for the footnote on reminders.

F009.name:
Family calendar read-only (

-calendar MCP)
F009.description: "What's on Saturday?" or "is anyone free Friday at 1?" is answered from the family Google Calendar, read-only; it also feeds the daily briefs.
F009.how: Host-side stdio MCP per person: gog mcp with --readonly exposes calendar_events; freebusy and conflicts need a thin wrapper; allow bundle-mcp in the sandbox gate; publish the OAuth app.
corrections: The 9 Oct wording has Tony hand-write the calendar MCP server. gogcli.sh/mcp.html documents a built-in stdio server (gog --account <account> mcp) with a read-only calendar_events tool and an --allow-tool filter, so listing events needs no custom code. Freebusy and conflicts exist only as CLI commands (gogcli.sh/commands) and still need a wrapper.

Catalog JSON 'needs' expects a calendar.readonly scope from --services calendar. The documented switch is --readonly on gog auth add; Google's scope list does include calendar.readonly (developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/auth). The Markdown asked to verify the flag; gog's command page confirms it.
unverified: gog is not installed on this Mac, so its flags were read from gogcli.sh and not from the binary; the bundled skill names the brew formula gogcli while the site shows a tap-qualified name.
Whether gog's calendar_events MCP tool can be pinned to a single calendar id was not confirmed.
Google or iCloud is still Tony's open decision; the iCloud route needs the OpenClaw macOS app paired as a node, which is not installed.

sources.title: Configuration — tool policy
sources.supports: Configured MCP servers are plugin-owned tools that sandboxed sessions only see when the sandbox tool allowlist includes bundle-mcp or the server's tool names.

sources.title: gogcli docs: MCP server
sources.supports: gog ships its own stdio MCP server whose only Calendar tool is a read tool that lists events; write tools stay hidden unless explicitly allowed.

sources.title: gogcli command reference: gog auth add
sources.supports: Adding an account with the read-only flag requests read-only OAuth scopes and blocks mutating requests at runtime.

sources.title: Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Google APIs (Google for Developers)
sources.supports: An external OAuth app left in Testing status gets refresh tokens that expire after seven days, so the app must be published for an always-on agent.

F010.name: Calendar event create with approval (or .ics tap-to-add)
F010.description: Happy drafts an event from a message or flyer: first as a calendar file the parent taps to add, later a direct calendar write after an explicit approve.
F010.how: Step 1: small plugin emits an .ics attachment. Step 2: write MCP wrapping gog calendar create with a separate write token; before_tool_call returns requireApproval (10-minute cap), rejects attendees.
corrections: A 9 Oct note says gog has no delete command. That holds only for the bundled skill text; the gog command index (gogcli.sh/commands) lists gog calendar delete, and gog calendar create accepts --attendees and --send-updates, so the write wrapper must leave delete out and strip those flags itself.
unverified: That Messages on iPhone offers to add an event when an .ics attachment is tapped: Apple's guide documents .ics import from Mail and by link, and the page body could not be read by the fetch tool.
That an .ics file passes OpenClaw's outbound media checks on iMessage (reference/rich-output-protocol.md:22) was not tested.
The in-house .ics generator plugin and the write wrapper do not exist yet.

Typing /approve in iMessage Basic mode to resolve a plugin approval was not tested end to end; the docs say channels without interactive controls fall back to plain-text /approve (exec-approvals-advanced.md:299).

sources.title: gog skill (bundled with OpenClaw)
sources.supports: The bundled gog skill documents creating a calendar event from the command line.

sources.title: Plugin permission requests
sources.supports: A plugin approval waits two minutes by default and ten at most, after which the call is blocked, so the parent must approve promptly or Happy must propose again.

sources.title: Events: insert (Google Calendar API reference)
sources.supports: Creating an event needs a write scope such as calendar.events, and guests are only notified when sendUpdates asks for it, so an event without attendees contacts nobody.

sources.title: RFC 5545: Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar)
sources.supports: The .ics file is the standard iCalendar format whose event component carries title, start and end, which a small generator can emit.

F011.name: Snap-to-action: photo or PDF dates become reminder and calendar proposals
F011.description: After reading a flyer, slip or schedule, Happy lists the dates it found and offers reminders or calendar entries; nothing is written until the parent says yes.
F011.how: Prompt-level standing order on top of F002 and F007 (F010 for calendar); plain conversational proposal rather than ask_user, whose wait is 900 seconds by default; llm-task optional.
corrections: Catalog JSON 'needs' relies on ask_user for the confirmation. ask-user.md:181 says not to use it to confirm a plan, and its wait is clamped to one hour at most (ask-user.md:116-117). The Markdown already switches to a plain proposal.
unverified: Date extraction accuracy on real flyers (missing years, two children, blurry photos) has not been measured.
The remark that iPhone Live Text already offers add-to-calendar for a single date was not sourced.
End-to-end behaviour of the calendar half was not assessed because it waits on F010; the reminder half needs only F001, F002 and F007.

sources.title: Ask user
sources.supports: The ask_user tool is not meant for confirming the agent's own plan, so the yes-or-no step should be an ordinary chat proposal.

sources.title: Media understanding
sources.supports: Text extracted from an attached file reaches the model wrapped in untrusted-content markers, which supports treating flyer text as data and confirming before any write.

sources.title: LLM task
sources.supports: Schema-validated JSON extraction exists as an optional bundled plugin tool that must be enabled and allowed; this feature does not require it.

sources.title: Automation payloads (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A job created by an agent can never hold more tools than the turn that created it, which bounds what a chat-created return-by reminder could do.

sources.title: What is Costco's return policy? - Costco Customer Service
sources.supports: The 90-day return window applies to a listed set of electronics and major appliances; other merchandise falls under an open-ended satisfaction guarantee.

sources.title: Publication 502, Medical and Dental Expenses - IRS
sources.supports: The IRS publication is the authority on which medical costs qualify, which is what any FSA eligibility hint would have to be checked against.

F012.name: Birthday, anniversary and gift-date heads-up
F012.description: A week before a birthday, anniversary, teacher-gift date or dentist recall each parent gets one line, with last year's gift note when one was recorded.
F012.how: Dates table rendered into each parent's memory folder; daily isolated automation announces to the owner; or a command payload script that computes the window with no model call.
corrections: Catalog JSON promises 'zero new tools' using wiki_search and wiki_apply on a weekly Monday job. memory-wiki has to be enabled first (memory-wiki.md:20-23), and a weekly run with a seven-day lead gives 7 to 13 days of notice. The Markdown already uses a dates file and a daily job.
unverified: The family dates table does not exist yet; someone has to enter the dates.
That phone contacts and calendars already surface birthdays was not sourced.
That memory-wiki is not enabled today comes from the 9 Oct plugin list, not from a live check.

sources.title: Automation payloads
sources.supports: A scheduled command payload runs a script on the gateway host and delivers its output with no model call, which is enough for a date-window check.

sources.title: User model
sources.supports: Cron sessions do not get MEMORY.md injected, so the dates must be searchable or embedded in the job itself.

sources.title: Memory wiki
sources.supports: The wiki tools the original idea used belong to a bundled plugin that has to be enabled first.

sources.title: Automation schedules
sources.supports: A top-of-hour cron job is staggered by up to five minutes unless exact timing is requested, which is fine for a morning heads-up.

F013.name: Weekday morning brief (07:00, no mail yet)
F013.description: Each parent gets one short weekday 07:00 text: weather and alerts, today's calendar, items due, trash day and sunset; mail stays in a separate digest.
F013.how:
Isolated automation per parent on

-main: `"0 7 * * 1-5" --tz`, explicit `--tools home_weather,

-calendar__*`, no `--light-context`, no web tools, `--announce --to imessage:`.
unverified: The 9 Oct note names ChatGPT Pulse as a current peer; a search summary in this run said OpenAI retired Pulse in favour of scheduled tasks in June 2026, but OpenAI's release-notes page returned HTTP 403, so its current status is unconfirmed.

The catalog passes `home-store__*` in `--tools`; the installed docs document the `<server>__<tool>` prefix only for MCP servers, and home-store is planned as a native plugin, so that glob is untested.
That the NWS forecast endpoints carry no sunrise or sunset field: the opened documentation page does not list one, absence was not proven.
The weather plugin's current fields (12-hour periods, alerts without id, no sunset) were read in ~/src/happy-config/plugins/home-weather/nws.js, which is not one of the two citable source kinds.
Alexa+ as a peer product was not opened in this run.

sources.title: CLI reference: automations (cron)
sources.supports: The installed CLI creates a scheduled agent job from a cron expression such as 07:00 daily, pinned to one agent.

sources.supports: Scheduled sessions do not get MEMORY.md, so the brief's facts must live in the job prompt or AGENTS.md.

sources.title: Automation delivery

sources.title: Gemini Apps Help: Schedule actions in Gemini Apps

-main writes into the task text.

F030.name: Shared Apple Reminders lists and Family Notes folder bridge
F030.description: Happy can read, add to and tick off items on the Reminders lists the family already shares, so changes show up on both parents' iPhones.
F030.how: In-house host-side tool plugin wrapping remindctl (list/add/complete, named lists only, no delete); happy's Apple Account joins the shared lists; Reminders permission granted in the gateway's own process context.
unverified: No opened source confirms that remindctl can add to or complete items on a shared iCloud list owned by another family member; its README only says reminders sync through the normal iCloud path.
Which binary macOS records the Reminders permission against when the launchd gateway spawns remindctl is not documented in any opened source; it needs one test on happy's logged-in desktop.
The Notes half (appending to a shared folder with osascript) has no first-party Apple scripting reference opened in this run; the memo CLI page only confirms it relies on AppleScript and an editor.

sources.title: Tool plugins (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: OpenClaw has a supported way to build a small plugin that only adds typed agent tools, which is the shape of the planned home-reminders bridge.

sources.title: steipete/remindctl README
sources.supports: The CLI lists, adds, completes and deletes Apple Reminders with JSON output, needs macOS 14 or later, and needs Reminders access granted to the app that runs it on that Mac.

sources.title: Device commands (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The node reminders commands are offered by iOS and Android nodes only, and adding a reminder is a dangerous command that needs an explicit gateway allow, so a macOS node is not an alternative path.

sources.title: Share a reminder list on Mac - Apple Support
sources.supports: A shared list lives in iCloud Reminders, invitees must accept and also use iCloud Reminders, and accepted participants can create and edit items from any of their devices.

F031.name: Household structured store (home-store MCP: schedules, ledgers, lists)
F031.description: A small household database for dated schedules and simple facts (filter every 90 days, last oil change) that both parents' agents can read and update.
F031.how: In-house defineToolPlugin over node:sqlite with schedule_get/upsert/mark_done and fact_get/set; allowlisted on both mains and in tools.sandbox.tools; secret check inside execute or via definePluginEntry.
corrections: The 9 Oct verifier note says the secret-rejecting before_tool_call hook can live in the same plugin as the defineToolPlugin store. docs/plugins/tool-plugins.md:11 says defineToolPlugin adds tools only, and :233 points to definePluginEntry when tools are combined with hooks.

The catalog chooses defineToolPlugin for the store but still names its tools home-store__schedule_* in the automations. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:242 gives that server__tool form to MCP servers only; a plugin's tools carry the names it declares, so job tool lists must use those.
unverified: node:sqlite is labelled release candidate on nodejs.org; no long-run test of it inside the gateway process was done.

sources.title: Tool plugins (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A defineToolPlugin plugin adds agent-callable tools only (no hooks or services), which fits a local store with a handful of typed tools.

sources.title: SQLite | Node.js documentation
sources.supports: Node ships a built-in synchronous SQLite module (added in 22.5.0, release-candidate stability), so the store needs no extra database dependency on the installed Node 26.

sources.title: Multi-agent sandbox and tools (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The double-underscore server__tool name belongs to configured MCP servers; a native plugin tool is addressed by the name it declares.

F032.name: Grocery and errand capture by text or voice, plus Saturday shop list
F032.description: Parents text 'add oat milk' any time; on Saturday morning each parent gets the open shopping list in one message.
F032.how: F030 reminders tools for capture; one isolated automation per parent (--cron, --tools, --announce on imessage); voice capture needs channels.imessage.includeAttachments plus transcription.
unverified: Flagging staples not bought in three weeks needs completion history; no opened source shows remindctl or Reminders exposing it, so it would need its own log in the F031 store.
Local voice transcription was not tested; by default the installed stack would send a voice memo to the configured cloud provider.

sources.title: Standing orders (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A scheduled job is created with a cron expression, a timezone and an announce target on the iMessage channel, which is the shape of the Saturday list message.

sources.title: Automation payloads (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A scheduled job can be limited to a named list of tools, so the Saturday run can hold only the list-reading tool.

sources.title: iMessage media and attachments (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Voice memos and photos are dropped before the agent sees them unless inbound attachments are switched on, which is off on this install.

sources.title: Create grocery lists in Reminders on your iPhone - Apple Support
sources.supports: The iPhone already sorts a Groceries-type list into store sections by itself (iOS 17 or later with iCloud Reminders), so Happy adds little to capture and sorting.

F033.name: Sunday meal plan to grocery list (with recipe box)
F033.description: On Sunday afternoon the cook gets five dinner ideas fitted to the week's calendar and allergies; a reply swaps a night or adds missing ingredients to the list.
F033.how: Isolated automation reads recipes and calendar, saves the plan (store row or wiki synthesis) for the main session to use on reply; ask_user is main-session only; no ordering.
unverified: It depends on the calendar connection (F009) and the Reminders bridge (F030), neither of which exists yet.
The 9 Oct statement that AI meal-plan features have poor retention has no source opened in this run.

sources.title: Automation payloads (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Each isolated run starts a fresh session with no earlier conversation, so the Sunday job has to save the plan somewhere the parent's main session can read when they reply.

sources.title: Ask user (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The structured question tool is not given to scheduled or other non-primary runs, so the plan message can only invite a normal reply.

sources.title: openclaw wiki CLI reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The wiki write path creates or refreshes a synthesis page with a managed body, which is how a recipe or the week's plan could be stored without free-form page edits.

sources.title: Food Shopping and Meal Planning | Nutrition.gov (USDA)
sources.supports: Planning the week's meals first and deriving the grocery list from the plan is the standard household method that USDA's nutrition portal points families to.

F034.name: Home systems and service-provider registry with lookup
F034.description: Send a photo of an appliance's data plate once; later ask what filter the furnace takes or who fixed the boiler and get the stored answer.
F034.how: includeAttachments on; the vision model reads the plate; the agent saves a wiki synthesis page (wiki_apply) or a store fact; manual PDFs by URL go through the research agent.
unverified: That gpt-6-sol accepts images on Tony's custom provider ids was not checked in this run.
The memory-wiki route needs that bundled plugin enabled (F043 step 2); with only the shared Markdown folder, the operator types the plate details in by hand.

sources.title: iMessage media and attachments (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Photos sent over iMessage reach the agent only after inbound attachments are enabled; today they are dropped.

sources.title: Media understanding (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: When the reply model accepts images, the original photo is passed to it directly, so reading a data plate needs no extra tool.

sources.title: openclaw wiki CLI reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The agent's only wiki write is creating or refreshing a synthesis page or editing metadata, so one synthesis page per appliance is the write shape; entity pages are seeded by the operator.

sources.title: PDF tool (OpenClaw docs)
sources.anchor: rejected when the tool runs sandboxed
sources.supports: A sandboxed agent cannot hand the pdf tool a remote URL, so fetching a manual from the web is a job for the separate research agent, not the parent's main agent.

F036.name: Babysitter / grandparent sheet
F036.description: 'Make the sitter sheet for Friday' returns one message with bedtimes, allergies, medicines and emergency contacts for the parent to forward.
F036.how: Prompt template referenced from AGENTS.md over F043 facts (plus calendar once connected); mains hold no message tool, so nothing is sent; the Wi-Fi password is never stored.
unverified: 'Tonight's plan' needs the calendar connection (F009), which is not built yet.

sources.title: Babysitting Reminders: Checklist for Parents & Sitters - HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics)
sources.supports: The paediatricians' own checklist lists what parents should always leave with a sitter (parent, neighbour, doctor and emergency contacts, address), which is the content of the sheet.

sources.title: Standing orders (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Only the top-level bootstrap files are loaded each session, so a sitter template kept in a subfolder must be pointed to from AGENTS.md.

sources.title: Tool policy (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Sending is a separate tool (message) that an agent only has if granted; without it the sheet can only come back as the reply to the asking parent.

sources.title: Plugin hooks: tool policy (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The tool-call hook sees tool names and parameters, not reply text, so it cannot scrub a password from an answer; the control is never storing the password.

F037.name: Draft-only outreach texts (vendors, coaches, carpool parents)
F037.description: Ask for a text to the plumber, the coach or the carpool parents and get ready-to-paste wording; the parent sends it from their own phone.
F037.how:
Prompt-only on

-main: no message tool is granted and iMessage Basic mode is plain send/receive to the allowlisted family; vendor names come from F034.
unverified: Using tomorrow's calendar in a draft needs the calendar connection (F009), which is not built yet.

sources.title: Tool policy (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Outbound sending is one named tool; an agent that is not granted it can only answer the person who asked, which is what keeps this drafts-only.

sources.title: iMessage private API (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: With SIP left on, the channel offers text and media send plus receive only, so there is no richer action surface to worry about.

F038.name: Home upkeep calendar: maintenance, car care, bins, seasonal nudges
F038.description: Nudges for filter changes, car inspection, seasonal jobs and bins the night before pickup; 'did the furnace filter' updates the record.
F038.how: Per-parent isolated automations (--cron, --tz, --tools) over the F031 schedule tools; the run answers NO_REPLY when nothing is due; holiday shifts come from a table entered once.
corrections: The catalog writes this job's tools as home-store__schedule_*. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:242 gives that double-underscore form to MCP servers; if F031 ships as a defineToolPlugin, the job must list the plugin's own tool names instead.
unverified: The opened scheduler docs show no holiday calendar; the holiday bin shift relies on the agent reading a table, which was not tested.
The 90-day filter interval in the catalog is a household choice; the ENERGY STAR page opened here says to check monthly.

sources.title: openclaw automations CLI reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Jobs take a standard cron expression with a named timezone, enough for 'first of the month' and 'night before pickup' schedules.

sources.title: Automation payloads (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: An unattended run that finds nothing to do returns the silent token and no message is delivered, so a daily check stays quiet until something is due.

sources.title: Maintenance Checklist | ENERGY STAR
sources.supports: The US government efficiency programme advises checking the HVAC filter monthly and a yearly pre-season service, so recurring upkeep reminders reflect real maintenance guidance.

sources.title: About New York State Inspections - NY DMV
sources.supports: A registered vehicle needs a safety inspection once a year, which makes the per-car inspection month a real recurring date worth tracking.

sources.title: ReCollect terms of service
sources.anchor: phone call or mobile app notification
sources.supports: ReCollect lets residents sign up for collection reminders by email, text message, phone call or app notification.

sources.title: Home Assistant: ReCollect Waste integration
sources.supports: Municipalities on ReCollect usually offer a calendar subscription whose URL carries place and service ids, and the JSON endpoint the integration uses is not an official ReCollect API.

sources.title: Automation schedules
sources.supports: Cron schedules can be pinned to an IANA timezone, which the night-before bins line needs.

adds: If the town or hauler uses ReCollect, its address-specific pickup calendar replaces the hand-typed bins table; ReCollect already sends its own reminders, so Happy only folds the line into the evening brief.

F039.name: Kids' chore rota and after-school routine board (parent-run)
F039.description: A parent-run chore and after-school board: Sunday overview, weekday routine lines to the on-duty parent, a quick 'dishes done' to mark it, Saturday tally.
F039.how: Same automation primitives as F038 over F031 rows; school-holiday skip by returning NO_REPLY; the kids are not users, so parents do every check-off.
unverified: Picking the on-duty parent needs the calendar connection (F009), which is not built yet.
The 9 Oct market rating for chore nudges has no source opened in this run; a paper chart on the fridge may simply be less effort.

sources.title: openclaw automations CLI reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: When a scheduled run returns only the silent token nothing is posted, which is the only way to skip a weekday on a school holiday since cron itself has no holiday rule.

sources.title: Automation payloads (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Each board job can be held to the store and calendar tools it needs.

sources.title: Age-Appropriate Chores for Children - HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics)
sources.supports: Paediatric guidance supports regular chores, charts or checklists and praise for school-age children, so a weekly rota for an 8 and a 10 year old is a reasonable thing to track.

F041.name: Durable per-person memory: 'remember this' write path, recall tools, and memory scopes
F041.description: 'Remember this' actually sticks: each parent's agent can save a fact to its own notes and find it again later.
F041.how:
Allow write/edit (deny apply_patch) on

-main with rw workspace; in-house before_tool_call hook limits paths to MEMORY.md, USER.md, memory/*.md; memory_search FTS-only; session-memory hook.
corrections: The catalog relies on `sessions_search` with visibility `agent` to find pre-reset conversations. docs/gateway/config-tools/sessions-and-subagents.md:58 says a sandboxed session stays limited to sessions it spawned while agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility is 'spawned' (the default); the mains run with sandbox mode all, so that key must change as well. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:372 adds that tools.sessions.visibility is gateway-wide, not per agent.
unverified: Whether visibility 'self' already reaches the same chat's pre-reset history (the docs define self as the current session key) was not tested.
The opened hook docs expose no taint flag, so 'refuse writes after web results' means the hook plugin tracking web tool calls itself; untested.
'Most-asked family-assistant request' has no source opened in this run.

sources.title: Memory overview (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The memory plugin gives the agent search, read and intent tools but no write tool, so saving a fact needs the general file tools.

sources.title: Tool policy (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Allowing write also enables apply_patch, and denying write does not deny it, so apply_patch has to be denied by name when only narrow file writes are wanted.

sources.title: Plugin hooks: tool policy (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A plugin hook sees each tool call's name and parameters and can block it, which is the mechanism for limiting writes to the memory files.

sources.title: Sessions and subagents config (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A sandboxed session can only reach sessions it spawned unless the sandbox session-tools setting is widened, whatever the gateway-wide visibility says.

F042.name: Family facts and preferences baked into USER.md from family.json5
F042.description: Both parents' agents start every chat already knowing the kids' school, routines and activities and each adult's standing preferences.
F042.how: Generator renders adult directives into USER.md (4,000-character cap) and kid and routine facts into MEMORY.md with trigger comments; nothing is rendered into shared agents.
unverified: The generator script and the family registry live in happy-config and were not opened in this run.
That a chat edit to a generated file is lost on the next deploy is a property of Tony's generator, not something an opened source states.

sources.title: User model (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: USER.md has a fixed small budget that config can only lower, so it cannot hold a full family fact sheet.

sources.title: Standing orders (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: USER.md and MEMORY.md are among the files injected at the start of every session, which is why generated facts are known without re-typing.

sources.title: Memory architecture (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A fact line can carry trailing trigger phrases so it is pulled in when a message is about that topic.

F043.name: Household knowledge vault (memory-wiki) with shared notes folder
F043.description: One shared family handbook both parents' agents can search: people, home systems, providers, renewal dates, sitter notes.
F043.how: Step 1: shared Markdown folder added to each main's memory.search.extraPaths. Step 2: enable bundled memory-wiki, vault.scope global, own vault dir; wiki_search/get/apply/lint on mains only.
unverified: The two installed pages disagree on whether enabling memory-wiki needs a gateway restart (docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md:26 says it applies to a running gateway, docs/cli/wiki.md:15 shows a restart).
That memory_search in a sandboxed main can read a shared folder outside its workspace was not tested.

sources.title: Memory configuration reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Extra folders to index can be set per agent and are combined with the global list, so only the two parent agents need to see the shared folder.

sources.title: Memory wiki (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The knowledge-vault plugin ships with OpenClaw and is switched on with one command.

sources.title: Memory architecture (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A fact line tagged with trigger phrases is injected automatically when a message matches strongly, at most three per turn, which is how an allergy line surfaces in a recipe chat.

F044.name: Document vault: 'file this' (insurance, warranties, manuals)
F044.description: 'File this as the car insurance policy' stores the PDF, keeps a short summary of the key dates and reminds a parent 30 days before it expires.
F044.how: New host tool copies the inbound attachment (includeAttachments on) to a fixed folder; pdf extracts text; `openclaw wiki ingest` takes the summary only; own expiry index; nightly --command automation.
unverified: No opened page shows a plugin tool resolving an inbound media reference by itself; that step needs a spike.
A policy document would be read by the cloud model for field extraction; whether that is acceptable is Tony's call.

sources.title: PDF tool (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The built-in PDF tool can read an attachment that arrived in chat by its managed inbound reference.

sources.title: openclaw wiki CLI reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Wiki ingest takes local Markdown or text only, so the PDF itself cannot go into the vault; only an extracted summary can.

sources.title: Memory wiki (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The listed claim fields contain no expiry date, so renewal dates need a separate index kept by the filing tool.

sources.title: openclaw automations CLI reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The scheduler can run a plain script on a schedule without starting a model turn, which suits a nightly expiry scan.

F045.name: Google Sheets and Drive read-only lookup
F045.description: Ask about the family's existing Google Sheets and Docs (chore chart, house projects) without moving them anywhere.
F045.how: Install gog, per-person OAuth; register `gog mcp` (write tools hidden by default; --allow-tool drive_search,drive_get,docs_get,sheets_read_range) with openclaw mcp add; allow only on that person's main.
corrections:
The catalog plans a custom `

-drive-ro` wrapper because gog was taken to be CLI-only. gogcli.sh/mcp documents `gog mcp`, a typed stdio MCP server exposing drive_search, drive_get, docs_get and sheets_read_range, so this feature needs no custom wrapper.

The 9 Oct note says no read-only option is documented for gog. The same upstream page documents that write tools stay hidden unless --allow-write is passed and that a read-only policy cannot be widened by it, and the gog README shows a global --readonly flag; the bundled skill file simply does not mention them.
unverified: gog is not installed, so which version ships `gog mcp` and which OAuth scopes it requests for Drive and Sheets were not checked locally; no first-party page opened here shows a read-only Drive scope choice at consent time.
Whether the family keeps anything useful in Sheets is unknown.

sources.title: gog skill (bundled with OpenClaw)
sources.supports: The bundled Google Workspace skill documents read commands for Sheets, Drive search and Docs, and also write commands, so access must be narrowed outside the skill.

sources.title: MCP server - gog documentation
sources.supports: gog ships its own stdio MCP server with fixed read tools for Drive, Docs and Sheets; write tools stay hidden unless explicitly allowed, and the tool set can be narrowed by name.

sources.title: Choose Google Drive API scopes (Google for Developers)
sources.supports: Google has a view-and-download-only Drive scope, and classes it as restricted, so even read-only Drive access is a high-sensitivity grant.

sources.title: Connect MCP servers (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: A local stdio MCP server is registered with a command and arguments and then probed, and its tools go through the normal per-agent tool policy.

F046.name: Semantic and multimodal memory search (local embeddings)
F046.description: Search notes by meaning ('the kid's nut thing' finds 'tree-nut allergy') with embeddings computed on the Mac mini; photo search stays unavailable locally.
F046.how: Install @openclaw/llama-cpp-provider, run the embedding-only setup, set memory.search.provider local with fallback none, reindex; image indexing still requires gemini-embedding-2 (cloud).
corrections: The catalog ties this to M2 (local models). docs/plugins/llama-cpp.md:123 documents an embedding-only setup that adds no chat model, so the text leg does not depend on M2 and can be done on the installed stack.

The 9 Oct reason for dropping photo search is that no local multimodal embedder exists. Google's EmbeddingGemma page now describes EmbeddingGemma 2 as multimodal and local; the actual block is that OpenClaw 2026.9.7 only indexes images with gemini-embedding-2 (docs/reference/memory-config.md:495).
unverified: Whether the managed llama.cpp server in 2026.9.7 can load EmbeddingGemma 2 was not checked.
The gain over keyword search for a few hundred family notes is a judgement, not a sourced figure.

sources.title: Builtin memory engine (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Local embeddings come from an installable official plugin plus a local provider setting pointing at a small GGUF embedding model.

sources.title: llama.cpp provider (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: There is an embedding-only setup that installs the managed server and embedding model without adding or changing any chat model.

sources.title: Memory configuration reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: Image and audio indexing works only with Google's cloud embedding model and only for files in the extra paths.

sources.title: EmbeddingGemma - Google AI for Developers
sources.supports: Google describes the first EmbeddingGemma as a small text-only model that runs on-device, and a newer version as a multimodal model that also runs locally.

F047.name:
Per-person read-only Gmail (

-gmail MCP)
F047.description: Each adult's own mail agent can search and read that adult's Gmail; nothing is changed, labelled or sent.
F047.how:
`gog mcp` as a host-side stdio entry under `mcp.servers`, read tools only, allowed per agent as `

-gmail__*`; authorize with `--gmail-scope readonly`.
corrections: The 9 Oct verifier note says gogcli has no read-only-only Gmail scope. The upstream command reference lists `--gmail-scope full|readonly|send|read-send` and says `--readonly` on `gog auth add` requests read-only OAuth scopes, so a read-only grant can be requested; the catalog's hedge 'if the installed version supports it' can be firmed up, pending a check on the installed binary.

The 9 Oct text treats the `

-gmail` wrapper as new code. Upstream gogcli ships a stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`) that exposes only read tools unless `--allow-write` is passed, so the config entry can run gog directly with an `--allow-tool` list and no wrapper.

The 9 Oct needs list stops at the per-agent allow list. With sandbox mode 'all' (Happy's setting) the installed docs add a second gate: MCP tools are filtered out unless `tools.sandbox.tools` also names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130).
unverified: gog is not installed on this Mac; the flags come from the upstream main-branch docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the version Homebrew installs.

Whether both adults' tokens would sit in one keyring under the happy user: upstream says tokens use the platform keyring by default with a file backend for headless hosts; splitting them with a per-adult GOG_HOME is my inference from the paths doc.
Refresh-token lifetime for a self-made Google OAuth client left in testing status was not checked in this run; Google's scope page does mark gmail.readonly as a Restricted scope.
The promptfoo injection canary is an in-house test, not an OpenClaw feature.

sources.title: Connect MCP servers
sources.supports: MCP server definitions live in gateway config and the tools they expose pass through the same tool profile and policy controls as built-in tools.

sources.title: Multi-agent sandbox and tools
sources.supports: MCP tools get server-prefixed names that per-agent allow and deny lists can target, deny always wins, and a server with no allowed tool is omitted for that agent.

sources.title: gogcli docs: MCP server
sources.supports: gog ships its own typed stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`); by default it registers read tools only (Gmail search, get message, get thread) and hides every write tool.

sources.title: gogcli command reference: gog auth add
sources.supports: The authorization command takes a Gmail scope mode of full, readonly, send or read-send, and its --readonly flag requests read-only OAuth scopes.

F048.name:
Per-person Gmail drafts (

-gmail-drafts MCP)
F048.description: Happy writes drafts into the owner's own Gmail Drafts folder; the owner reviews and sends from Gmail, and Happy has no way to send.
F048.how: `gog --gmail-no-send mcp --allow-write --allow-tool gmail_create_draft,gmail_update_draft`; fail-closed `before_tool_call` block on any send tool; CLI drafts thread with `--reply-to-message-id`.
corrections: The catalog says 'verify `--reply-to-message-id` on drafts create, else drafts are unthreaded'. The upstream command reference documents `--reply-to-message-id` and `--thread-id` on `gog gmail drafts create`, plus a separate `gog gmail drafts reply <messageId>`; the installed SKILL.md (line 59) merely omits them.

The catalog describes a custom MCP around `gog gmail drafts create` with the hook as the only send barrier. Upstream gog's own MCP server already keeps `gmail_send_message` and `gmail_send_draft` behind a separate `--allow-gmail-send` flag, so the hook is a second layer, not the only one.
unverified: Whether gog's MCP tool `gmail_create_draft` exposes the reply and thread parameters that the CLI command has; if not, threaded drafts need a thin wrapper over the CLI.
gog is not installed here; confirm the tool names with `gog mcp --allow-write --list-tools` after install.
The promptfoo 'send attempt is blocked' test is in-house.

sources.title: gogcli docs: MCP server
sources.supports: In gog's MCP mode the draft tools appear only with the write flag, the send tools need a separate send flag on top, and the no-send policy blocks sending while drafts still work.

sources.title: gogcli command reference: gog gmail drafts create
sources.supports: The draft-create command accepts a reply-to message id (and a thread id), which sets the reply headers and thread so the draft lands inside the conversation.

sources.title: Gmail API: Choose scopes
sources.supports: Google offers no drafts-only scope: the compose scope covers managing drafts and sending, and modify also includes sending, so the token itself can always send.

sources.title: Tool call policy hooks
sources.supports: A plugin's before_tool_call handler that returns a block is terminal, so a send tool can be denied in code the model cannot argue with.

F049.name: mailout: email the owner only ('email me this')
F049.description: 'Email me this': long answers, tables and plans land in the asker's own inbox from a dedicated family sender; nobody else can be a recipient.
F049.how:
Send-only tool over `gog gmail send` from a dedicated account; `before_tool_call` hook pins `to` to the requester's owner address, rejects cc/bcc, fails closed; `

-main` only.
unverified: That a parameter rewrite from before_tool_call is honoured for MCP-sourced tools: the doc states it for host-owned parameters and notes some native relays reject rewrites. Blocking is documented as terminal, so the safer build blocks unless the recipient equals the owner, or uses an in-house tool with no recipient parameter at all.
A daily send cap is in-house code; I found no built-in cap in the pages read.
Creating the dedicated family sender account and granting its send scope is a manual step outside OpenClaw.

sources.title: Bundled gog skill
sources.supports: The gog CLI sends mail with explicit to, subject and a body read from a file or stdin, which is the primitive the mailout tool wraps.

sources.title: Tool call policy hooks
sources.supports: A before_tool_call handler may return replacement parameters, which is how a recipient can be forced to the owner's address in code.

sources.title: gogcli docs: MCP server
sources.supports: In gog's MCP mode, sending is off unless a dedicated send flag is passed in addition to write access and tool selection.

F050.name: IMAP mailbox watch on a personal Gmail (allowlisted senders, per-message reader)
F050.description: Mail from a short list of trusted senders in an adult's Gmail is summarized per message by an isolated reader; other mail never reaches the model.
F050.how:
Bundled `imap` plugin, `allowedSenders`, `senderAuth.min: verified`, tool-less `

-mail-reader`; Google app password as SecretRef; texting the owner needs a hook-pinned `message` tool or a cron sweep.
unverified: Using Gmail labels as IMAP folders for per-topic watches (one account entry per mailbox) was not checked against a Google page.
Gmail IMAP IDLE support was not confirmed on a Google page; the plugin doc says it sweeps every pollSeconds in either mode.
Whether each allowlisted sender's mail passes aligned DMARC has to be tested sender by sender.
An app password is a whole-mailbox credential, broader than a read-only OAuth grant; this is my reading of Google's description, not a quoted statement.

sources.title: IMAP email trigger
sources.supports: The plugin checks the parsed From address against the account's sender allowlist before any message reaches a model; entries are full addresses or @domain, and an empty list disables the account.

sources.title: IMAP plugin manifest and config schema
sources.supports: The account schema has a boolean deliver (default false) and a password, but no channel or recipient field and no OAuth option, so the plugin cannot address an iMessage by itself.

sources.title: Automation webhooks
sources.supports: For hook agent turns with no destination, deliver true only allows a completion system event on the target agent's main session; it does not send a chat message to a person.

sources.title: Google Account Help: Sign in with app passwords
sources.supports: A Google app password needs 2-Step Verification on the account, is described by Google as not recommended, can be unavailable under some account protections, and is revoked when the account password changes.

F051.name: Dedicated school mailbox with isolated reader (school-mail) and forward-to-Happy
F051.description: A separate mailbox registered with school, PTA, coaches and the lunch system, read by an isolated reader, so no parent's private inbox is touched; parents can forward mail to it.
F051.how: Bundled `imap` plugin on a new mailbox (iCloud needs `watch.mode: "interval"`), allowlist includes both parents for forwards, tool-less reader; same delivery caveat as F050.
corrections: 'IMAP passes body text only' is slightly off: the plugin's prompt also lists attachment file names (dist/extensions/imap/index.js:55735). Contents of attached PDFs or images are still not passed, so flyer attachments remain unread.
unverified: Whether the district, PTA, coaches and lunch system each accept an extra or shared guardian address; this is a manual chore per system.

Auto-forwarding school mail from a parent's Gmail by filter may fail the plugin's aligned-DMARC check (Google's forwarding guidance says forwarded mail often fails SPF); DKIM survival was not tested, so registering the address directly is the safe route.
An iCloud+ custom-domain address with this plugin was not tested; Apple documents the IMAP host and app-specific passwords, not this combination.
The catalog marks this 'now' because it needs no private-inbox decision; I rate it 'build' because it needs a new mailbox, an app password and a reader agent entry.

sources.title: IMAP email trigger
sources.supports: Some iCloud servers do not advertise standard IDLE, so forcing interval polling (15 second minimum) is the supported path for an iCloud mailbox.

sources.title: IMAP plugin source: renderImapPrompt
sources.supports: The prompt handed to the reader contains From, Subject, a snippet, attachment file names and the capped text body; attachment contents are never included.

sources.title: Apple Support: iCloud Mail server settings for other email client apps
sources.supports: iCloud Mail is reachable over IMAP with SSL on port 993 and requires an app-specific password for third-party clients.

F052.name: 'Did I get an email about X?' lookup and thread summary
F052.description: 'Did the dentist confirm?' returns sender, date and gist, or a five-line thread timeline, from the asker's own inbox.
F052.how:
`

-main` calls `sessions_spawn` with `agentId` `

-mail` (allowed by `subagents.allowAgents`); the child searches with the read-only Gmail MCP and returns a bounded answer.
unverified:
That `

-main` currently lacks `sessions_spawn` in its allow list is taken from the 9 Oct notes; I did not re-read the live config.
'Quote only what was asked' is a prompt rule in AGENTS.md, not an enforced limit; the summary text does cross into the memory-holding agent.
Depends on F047 and G015, which are not built.

sources.title: Sub-agents: thread-bound sessions
sources.supports: A per-agent allowlist names which other configured agents may be targeted by an explicit agent id; the default is only the requester itself.

sources.title: Sub-agents: tool reference
sources.supports: The spawn tool takes an agent id so the child runs as the mail agent with that agent's own tool policy.

sources.title: Sub-agent tool policy
sources.supports: A spawned child can never use the message or scheduling tools, so the mail child cannot send anything itself and can only hand its answer back to the parent.

sources.title: Bundled gog skill
sources.supports: gog has a per-thread search and a per-message search, which cover both 'find the email' and 'walk the thread' lookups.

F053.name: Draft a reply or note (lands in Gmail Drafts)
F053.description: 'Reply to the plumber: Tuesday after 3 works' becomes a threaded draft in the owner's Gmail Drafts; the owner edits and sends.
F053.how: F048 drafts tool; `gog gmail drafts reply <messageId>` or `--reply-to-message-id` keeps the thread; absence and pickup templates in `AGENTS.md`; send stays blocked by hook.
corrections: The 9 Oct caveat that reply drafts may land unthreaded is resolved upstream: gogcli documents `gog gmail drafts reply <messageId>` and `--reply-to-message-id` on `drafts create`.
unverified: Whether gog's MCP draft tool exposes reply threading; if not, a thin wrapper around the CLI command is needed.
A reply draft inherits recipients from the thread, so an injected email could steer the To line; the owner must check it before sending. Design caveat, no source.
Per-adult voice and sign-off quality is model-dependent; not measured.

sources.title: gogcli command reference: gog gmail drafts reply
sources.anchor: Save a reply as a draft
sources.supports: gog has a dedicated command that stages a reply to a given message as a draft, with an option to leave out the quoted original.

sources.title: Ask user
sources.supports: The structured question tool exists only in the main session, so a tone question must be asked by the person's main agent before the hand-off, not by the mail child.

sources.title: Standing orders
sources.supports: Standing instructions such as reply templates belong in the agent's workspace file that is injected into every session.

sources.title: Tool call policy hooks
sources.supports: A plugin's before_tool_call handler that returns a block is terminal, so a send tool can be denied in code the model cannot argue with.

F054.name: Needs-reply tracker (both directions)
F054.description: A weekday list of people waiting on your reply and of your own unanswered emails; Gmail already shows both as nudges at the top of the inbox.
F054.how:
If built: isolated `automations` job at 17:30 weekdays on `

-mail`, Gmail searches via F047, `NO_REPLY` when empty. Gmail's Nudges setting already covers it.
unverified: False-positive rate on newsletters and no-reply senders was not measured.
Nudges require conversation view per the Gmail page; whether both adults have nudges switched on is unknown.

sources.title: Gmail Help: Reply to messages in Gmail
sources.supports: Gmail has two built-in nudge settings, one surfacing received mail you have not answered and one surfacing sent mail that may need a follow-up, both shown at the top of the inbox.

sources.title: Automation payloads

sources.title: Automation schedules

F054.reject_reason: A needs-reply tracker duplicates the nudges Gmail already shows at the top of the inbox.

F055.name: Urgent school alert relay (snow day, delay, early dismissal, bus, safety)
F055.description: A school closure, delay or early-dismissal email reaches both parents as one line; routine school mail stays quiet until the afternoon digest.
F055.how: F051 reader answers with an URGENT line or `NO_REPLY`; `deliver: true` texts nobody, so use a hook-pinned `message` tool (fast) or a 15-minute cron sweep.
unverified: Which notification system this district uses; ParentSquare is cited only as an example of a vendor that pushes urgent alerts itself.
End-to-end time from email arrival to iMessage was not measured; the plugin doc says the watcher sweeps every pollSeconds (default 60) and on IDLE notifications.
Accuracy of the URGENT versus ROUTINE split on real district mail is untested; a missed closure is the costly error.

sources.title: Automation webhooks

sources.title: Automation payloads

sources.title: Tool call policy hooks
sources.supports: The doc's own example hook inspects calls to the message tool and blocks disallowed ones, the pattern needed to admit only the two parents as recipients.

sources.title: ParentSquare: Help Please! Frequently Asked Parent Questions
sources.supports: A widely used school messaging vendor states that urgent alerts always reach parents by its own email, text and app channels, so the headline closure case is usually pushed already.

F056.name: School and activities mail digest (16:00), newsletter 5-liner, dated checklist, lunch-balance line
F056.description: Weekday afternoons both parents get a five-line text of the day's school and activity mail with dates spelled out, plus a dated to-do list with day-before reminders offered.
F056.how: `automations create '0 16 * * 1-5' --agent school-mail --session isolated --announce --to <chat>`, `--tools school-mail-ro__*`; read MCP is `gog mcp` (Gmail) or a himalaya wrapper (iCloud).
corrections: 'school-mail-ro MCP is gog (Gmail)' needs no wrapper code on the Gmail path: upstream gogcli ships a read-only stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`).
The built-in scheduling tool is listed as `automations`, with `cron` kept as an alias (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:73).
unverified: Whether himalaya has an MCP mode; its README does not mention one, so the iCloud path likely needs an in-house wrapper. The README also says native keyring support was removed in v2, so its password comes from a command.
That one job takes exactly one delivery target (hence two jobs or one group chat for two parents); I saw single-target examples only.
Groups are off today, so a family group chat target needs the iMessage group allowlist switched on first.
The home-store checklist, the F007 reminder path and the promptfoo newsletter eval are in-house pieces.
PDF or image newsletters are not read: the IMAP path passes attachment names only.

sources.title: Managing automation jobs
sources.supports: A recurring isolated job is created from a cron expression and prompt with a time zone, announce delivery, a channel and one explicit target.

sources.title: Automation payloads
sources.supports: Each job can be restricted to a named tool list, so the digest run sees only the mailbox read tool.

sources.title: iMessage: media and delivery targets
sources.supports: iMessage delivery accepts a stable chat id target, the recommended way to address one group thread holding both parents.

sources.title: Himalaya: CLI to manage emails
sources.supports: Himalaya is an IMAP command-line client installable with Homebrew that lists envelopes and reads messages, the read path for a non-Gmail school mailbox.

sources.supports: The gog CLI appends rows to a spreadsheet range from a JSON array.

sources.supports: The append command takes a spreadsheet id, a range, values as a JSON 2D array and an insert mode.

sources.title: MySchoolBucks: Help / FAQ
sources.supports: A school meal payment service documents an opt-in low-balance email per student, set by the parent, with a fixed small number of emails per episode.

sources.title: Prompt injection: What helps in practice
sources.supports: The docs recommend a tool-disabled reader agent to summarise untrusted content before anything with tools sees it.

sources.title: Web fetch
sources.supports: Plain fetch cannot read pages behind a login, so an account balance page is out of its reach.

sources.title: IMAP mail trigger: sender authentication
sources.supports: By default a message reaches the reader only when local verification finds an aligned DMARC pass for the allowlisted sender.

sources.title: The Seattle Public Library: Get Library Notifications (example public library)
sources.supports: Example of a public library that emails due-date, overdue and hold-ready notices to the address on each card, and notes that a third-party reminder service is being discontinued.

adds: The lunch-balance line comes from the lunch service's own low-balance email: a parent switches the alert on and lists the school mailbox as the alert address, because forwarded mail can fail the reader's sender check.
Library overdue and hold-ready notice emails as one more sender class for the digest; pre-due reminders depend on the library, and the full checked-out list stays in the library's own app.

F058.name: Package tracking: 'arriving today', delivered pings, return windows
F058.description: A morning 'arriving today' line and delivered pings built from carrier emails; USPS Informed Delivery, carrier apps and Gmail's own package tracking already do this.

UPS, FedEx and Amazon app notifications were not checked on vendor pages in this run.
Return-window extraction from order mail is model-dependent; no source.

sources.title: IMAP email trigger
sources.supports: By default only mail with locally verified, aligned DMARC is admitted, so each carrier's notification mail must pass that check or be silently rejected.

sources.supports: Gmail can read tracking numbers from order emails and show arrival date and delivery status in the inbox for participating US carriers.

sources.title: USPS: Informed Delivery
sources.supports: USPS offers a free service with a daily digest of incoming mail and optional text or email package status notifications.

F058.reject_reason: Package tracking from carrier emails duplicates the carrier apps, USPS Informed Delivery and Gmail's own package tracking.

F060.name: Appointment, refill, results and travel-change emails to .ics, reminders and alerts
F060.description: Appointment confirmations become a calendar file plus an evening-before reminder; pharmacy, results and flight-change emails become one-line pings; rebooking stays with a human.
F060.how: F050 watch for clinic, pharmacy and airline senders, `includeBody: false` for health senders; in-house .ics maker; `--at` reminder; file sent from `channels.imessage.attachmentRoots`.
corrections: 'Keep PHI senders subject-only (small maxBytes)': the plugin has an exact switch for this, `includeBody: false` per account entry (dist/extensions/imap/openclaw.plugin.json:232; index.js:55727), which drops body and snippet. `maxBytes` has a floor of 256, so a small value alone still passes the start of the body.

The 9 Oct note that the plugin 'already de-dups' needs a caveat: the doc says this path does not promise exactly-once processing after a crash (docs/automation/imap.md:158), so an occasional repeat or miss is possible.
unverified: That a .ics file sent through imsg Basic mode arrives as a tap-to-add calendar attachment; the installed docs describe outbound files in general and have no .ics handling.
Whether two IMAP account entries with different settings can watch the same mailbox (needed to treat health senders differently in one inbox).
Airline, pharmacy and clinic apps already push most of these alerts; not checked on vendor pages.
The .ics maker (F010) is in-house and not built.

sources.title: IMAP email trigger
sources.supports: Email bodies handed to the reader are capped by a per-account byte limit, and new messages are de-duplicated across gateway restarts.

F061.name: Tax document checklist (January to April)
F061.description: January to April, a Saturday digest of which expected tax forms have arrived by email and which are still missing; form contents are never opened.

Where the reader records 'form X available' between runs; needs an in-house store.
Sender domains for payroll, brokerage and the 529 plan, and whether their mail passes aligned DMARC.

F063.name: Renewals and expiry program (passports, licenses, registration, inspection, domains, Global Entry, filed documents)
F063.description: A monthly text lists what expires in the next 90 days (passports, inspection, registration, domains) with the lead time and official link; nothing is renewed or paid.
F063.how: Monthly isolated automation on the parent's agent with an empty tool list; the date table sits in the job message or AGENTS.md, generated from the family registry.
corrections: The kids' passports are not 'renewed': the federal page says a passport for a child under 16 is valid for 5 years and cannot be renewed, so the table row for each kid should say 'apply again in person, both kids present' and count on a 5-year cycle.
unverified: The two-year vehicle registration term: the state DMV renewal page opened in this run does not state the term.

Inspection, domain and Global Entry lead times are not backed by a listed source; the state DMV inspection page (every 12 months), ICANN's expiry-notice policy and the CBP renewal FAQ were opened but fall outside the four-source limit.
The 9-month passport lead time itself is a house choice built on the six-month rule plus processing time; no source sets that number.

sources.title: Automation payloads
sources.supports: An empty tool allowlist switches off every agent tool for the job, so the renewal table has to be in the prompt or bootstrap text rather than looked up at run time.

sources.title: User model
sources.supports: Cron sessions do not get MEMORY.md injected, so the table cannot live only in the memory vault.

sources.title: Renew an adult passport
sources.supports: Some countries and airlines refuse entry when a passport has under six months left, which is why the passport reminder needs a long lead time.

sources.title: Get a passport for a minor under 18
sources.supports: Passports for children under 16 last five years and cannot be renewed; the child must apply again in person with a parent.

sources.supports: The AAP's parent site lists a well-child visit at each year of age from 3 through 21.

sources.supports: The schedule is the AAP and Bright Futures consensus list of screenings and assessments recommended at each well-child visit.

sources.title: CDC: Recommended Vaccines for Older Children

sources.title: American Family Physician, August 2026: practice alert on the child and adolescent immunization schedule
sources.supports: The federal schedule was revised on 5 January 2026, moving influenza and several other vaccines to shared decision-making; the revision was removed from the CDC site on 16 March 2026 after a court stay; the AAP issued its own schedule, which other medical bodies endorsed.

sources.title: Web fetch
sources.supports: web_fetch is a plain GET without JavaScript, so a site that refuses plain fetches will refuse the research agent as well.

sources.title: IRS FAQ: Estimated tax, individuals
sources.supports: Individual estimated tax payments are due 15 April, 15 June, 15 September and 15 January of the following year, moving to the next business day when needed.

sources.title: IRS Publication 969: Health Savings Accounts and Other Tax-Favored Health Plans
sources.supports: Health FSA balances are forfeited at plan-year end unless the plan offers either a grace period of up to two and a half months or a limited carryover, and it cannot offer both.

sources.title: IRS Publication 503: Child and Dependent Care Expenses
sources.supports: Care counts for a child under 13, day camp may be a qualifying expense, overnight camp is not, and employer dependent-care benefits are excludable up to a yearly dollar limit.

sources.title: IRS: Online tax calendar
sources.supports: The IRS calendar is presented as quarterly pages with a print option and shows no calendar subscription, so there is no feed to consume.

adds: A yearly well-visit nudge per child from the AAP schedule; vaccine specifics are left to the pediatrician because the federal childhood schedule changed twice in 2026.
The child passport rule row: issued under 16 means five-year validity, no renewal, and a new in-person application with the parents present.
IRS estimated-tax dates (only if the family pays them) and the plan-specific FSA and dependent-care deadlines, typed in by a parent from the employer's plan document.

The duplicate check (statement versus later provider bill) only works if a parent logs every statement; no source shows families keep that up.
