F072.name: Kids agent base: per-kid iMessage handle, no tools, no memory, classifiers
F072.description: Each child texts Happy from their own Apple account and gets a tool-less, memory-less helper with safety checks both ways; cannot ship until a local model exists.
F072.how: bindings[] by DM handle to one agent per kid; minimal profile plus deny session_status and gateway; in-house classifier plugin on before_dispatch and message_sending; memory.search off; daily reset.
corrections: 'OpenAI terms are 13+, no cloud shortcut' could not be confirmed as worded: OpenAI's consumer Terms of Use returned HTTP 403 in this run, and the API page that did open sets no flat 13+ bar. It says personal data of children under 13 must not be processed without zero data retention and that COPPA applies. Keeping kids off the cloud stays the family's rule; store:false was not shown to count as zero data retention.
unverified: Llama Guard 3 as the classifier is the roadmap's choice and appears nowhere in the installed OpenClaw docs (its Ollama library page is cited under G019).
Whether kids admitted by pairing are refused as approvers; the roadmap itself marks this as untested.
How accurate any local classifier is on questions from 8 and 10 year olds; no evaluation exists yet.

sources.title: iMessage access control and routing
sources.supports: An iMessage binding can match one sender's handle, which is how each kid's messages would reach their own agent.

sources.title: Configuration — tool policy
sources.supports: The minimal tool profile still includes two tools, so a truly tool-less kids agent needs explicit denies on top.

sources.title: Message and delivery hooks
sources.supports: Plugins can claim an inbound message before the model (before_dispatch, same page line 15) and rewrite or cancel an outgoing reply, the two places a safety classifier attaches.

sources.title: Under-18 guidance
sources.supports: OpenAI tells API developers not to process personal data of children under 13 without zero data retention and to comply with COPPA.

F073.name: Homework hints and curiosity Q&A (explain, don't answer)
F073.description: A child asks a homework or curiosity question and gets grade-level hints and a short answer, never a finished worksheet; waits for the kids agent and a local model.
F073.how: Hint-first rules and grade band in the kid agent's AGENTS.md (channel sessions omit MEMORY.md); replies carry no URLs, or a short allowlist enforced by a message_sending hook.
unverified: 'Refuse whole-worksheet answers' is a prompt rule; no source shows a model holds to it when a child pushes.
A parent asking the same questions from their own chat works today, but that is the parent using the cloud model, not the child.

sources.title: Agent workspace
sources.supports: AGENTS.md is injected at the start of every session, so the hint-first rules and grade band are always present with no tools.

sources.title: User model
sources.supports: Channel sessions do not load MEMORY.md, so the rules and any approved link list must live in AGENTS.md.

sources.title: Message and delivery hooks
sources.supports: An outgoing-message hook can cancel a reply, the mechanical way to block any link outside an approved list.

sources.title: Complying with COPPA: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.supports: US law requires verifiable parental consent before an online service collects personal information from children under 13, the reason the plan keeps kids' chat off general cloud services.

F074.name: Practice drills: spelling lists, math facts, reading buddy and bedtime story
F074.description: Spelling, math-fact and reading rounds with a running score for the kids; blocked for kid-direct use, but a parent can run the same drills from their own chat today.
F074.how: Prompt program; score lives in the session until the daily reset; spoken spelling words need per-agent agents.entries.*.tts with the local say command, never cloud speech for kids.
unverified: Whether a spoken reply arrives as a playable voice message or as a file in iMessage Basic mode; the roadmap lists this as still to verify.
The quality of the macOS say voice for spelling words was not tried.

sources.title: Text-to-speech configuration
sources.supports: Speech can be produced by a local command-line program, shown with the macOS say command, so no cloud voice service is needed.

sources.title: Session management
sources.supports: With a daily reset the session, and the score inside it, lasts until the configured hour, 4 by default.

sources.title: Enabling the imsg private API
sources.supports: With SIP on, iMessage still sends and receives text and media, which is enough to deliver an audio reply.

F075.name: Kid-safe weekly card baked into the kids agent
F075.description: Kids ask 'what day is soccer' or 'whose turn to feed the dog' from a sanitised weekly card holding schedule, chores and first names only; waits for the kids agent.
F075.how: Weekly host job writes a '## This week' section into the kid agent's AGENTS.md, since channel sessions omit MEMORY.md and the extra-files hook only loads standard bootstrap names.
unverified: That a shared Apple family calendar on the kid's device already answers 'what day is soccer': the Apple page fetched returned only navigation text.
The wiki plugin and a calendar reader are not enabled today, so the card's data sources do not exist yet.

sources.title: User model
sources.supports: A card exported into MEMORY.md would never reach a child texting in, because channel sessions leave root memory out.

sources.title: Bundled hooks
sources.supports: The extra bootstrap files hook only loads files with the standard bootstrap names, so the card must be an AGENTS.md section or an AGENTS.md in a subfolder.

sources.title: Memory wiki
sources.supports: Wiki pages carry a privacy tier and anything not public is listed in a privacy review report, which the export can use as its deploy gate.

sources.title: Agent workspace
sources.supports: Bootstrap files are capped at 20,000 characters each by default, ample for a one-week card.

F076.name: Hue lights: rooms and scenes by name
F076.description: Text Happy to switch Hue rooms and scenes by name or ask which lights are still on, within a room allowlist and quiet hours enforced in code.
F076.how: In-house plugin wraps the openhue CLI on the host inside a sandboxed, stateless home agent reached by sessions_spawn; bridge key sits in ~/.openhue/config.yaml; Local Network permission for node.
unverified: Philips Hue's own local API documentation sits behind a developer login and was not opened; only the OpenHue CLI pages were.
Whether the launchd-run gateway needs the Local Network switch for plain HTTPS to the bridge; the bundled skills document it only for Sonos discovery.
The bridge's presence on the LAN comes from the 9 Oct scan and was not re-checked (no LAN contact in this run).

sources.title: OpenHue CLI (bundled skill)
sources.supports: The bundled skill documents the room, brightness and scene commands the plugin would wrap, plus the one-time bridge button pairing.

sources.title: Setup
sources.supports: The OpenHue setup command pairs by pressing the bridge button and saves the bridge address and key in a config file under the user's home folder, not the Keychain.

sources.title: Thread-bound sub-agent sessions
sources.supports: A sandboxed agent cannot hand off to an unsandboxed one, so the new home agent must be sandboxed like the parent agents that call it.

sources.title: Control access to your local network on Mac
sources.supports: macOS gates each app's ability to find and talk to devices on the home network behind a Privacy and Security switch.

F077.name: Sonos: play, pause, volume, what is playing
F077.description: Text Happy to play a Sonos favourite, pause everything, set a room's volume or group rooms, with a hard volume cap and quiet-hours cap enforced in code.
F077.how: In-house plugin wraps the sonos CLI (Homebrew steipete/tap/sonoscli) in the home agent; favourites only; needs Local Network permission for the gateway's node process or --ip per speaker.
corrections: 'sonoscli is go install only' is wrong: the project's install page recommends Homebrew (a steipete tap) and also offers prebuilt release archives; go install needs Go 1.26 or later. Only the bundled skill's metadata is limited to go install, so Go does not have to be installed on the Mac mini.
unverified: The volume caps (35, and 10 at night) are design numbers, not sourced.
The two speakers and their room names come from the 9 Oct scan and were not re-checked.

sources.title: Sonos CLI (bundled skill)
sources.supports: The bundled skill documents status, play, pause and per-room volume commands for the sonos CLI.

sources.title: Install — sonoscli
sources.supports: The project's own install page lists a Homebrew tap as the recommended route, with go install and prebuilt archives as alternatives.

sources.title: sonoscli README (raw)
sources.supports: sonoscli saves, lists and applies scenes, searches linked services through Sonos without Spotify Web API credentials, and describes itself as unofficial.

sources.title: sonoscli
sources.supports: A Homebrew formula exists, so the tool does not have to be built with Go.

adds: Named Sonos scenes from an allowlist and play-by-search through the music service already linked in the Sonos app, so Happy holds no music login; scenes must be saved in the happy account; a Homebrew install replaces the Go toolchain; auto-playing the first search hit has no content filter.

F078.name: Run an allowlisted macOS Shortcut (HomeKit / anything bridge)
F078.description: Tony builds Shortcuts on the Mac mini (goodnight, TV off) and Happy runs only the ones on an exact-name allowlist; never locks, garage, alarm or gate.
F078.how: Plugin tool calls 'shortcuts run <name>' on the host, no free-text input; Shortcuts live in the happy account, whose Apple Account is invited to the Home; requireApproval gates first runs.
unverified: That the command needs the happy user's logged-in desktop session and one interactive first run to clear privacy prompts; Apple's command-line page does not say.
Whether sharing the Home requires a home hub; search results suggest so but the fetched Apple page did not state it.
The LG TV being the only HomeKit accessory comes from the 9 Oct scan.

sources.title: Run shortcuts from the command line

sources.title: Share control of your home
sources.supports: A Home owner can invite another Apple Account to control accessories, the step the agent's own account needs before a Shortcut can touch HomeKit.

sources.title: Tool call policy hooks
sources.supports: A plugin hook can pause a tool call and ask for approval, which /approve resolves, giving a gate on the first run of a newly allowlisted Shortcut.

sources.title: Building plugins

sources.title: Automate tasks using AppleScript and Terminal on Mac (Apple Support)

sources.title: Plugin entry points
sources.supports: The plugin SDK provides a helper for plugins that add typed tools.

sources.supports: When interpreters such as osascript are allowlisted for exec, inline evaluation forms should require explicit approval.

sources.title: macOS permissions: Accessibility for Node runtimes
sources.supports: An Accessibility grant on the node binary applies to everything launched by that runtime.

sources.title: Tool plugins
sources.supports: The helper builds a plugin that only adds agent-callable tools.

F079.name: Camera snapshot and package-at-the-door watch
F079.description: Ask 'did the package come?' and get a one-line answer with a camera frame; nothing to point it at today, since the house has no local-stream camera.
F079.how: Plugin wraps camsnap snap for an outdoor camera allowlist, returns the JPEG as a structured attachment under channels.imessage.attachmentRoots; camsnap keeps camera passwords in a plain-text config file.
unverified: That Ring, Nest and Arlo cameras offer no local stream: only community forum posts were found for Ring, no first-party statement was opened.
'No RTSP camera in the house' comes from the 9 Oct scan and was not re-checked.
Frames would go to the cloud vision model; whether that is acceptable for pictures of the kids is a family decision.

sources.title: steipete/camsnap
sources.supports: The tool's own README says its config file holds camera credentials in plain text with user-only permissions, and that Homebrew is the install route.

sources.title: iMessage media and attachments
sources.supports: An outbound attachment path must sit under an allowed root, so the snapshot folder has to be added there.

sources.title: Rich output protocol
sources.supports: Plugins must return media through structured attachment fields, not text commands.

F080.name: Print it: PDFs, photos and generated pages to the home printer (incl. Sunday fridge sheet)
F080.description: 'Print this' sends a PDF, photo or https link to the home printer from anywhere, with a copies cap; the weekly fridge sheet waits for calendar and lists.
F080.how: Plugin calls lp -d <queue> -n <copies> on the host after lpadmin adds the queue once; the plugin downloads links itself because web_fetch returns text; attachments need includeAttachments.
unverified: That the Canon PRO-100 supports AirPrint or driverless IPP: no Canon page was opened. If it does, every phone in the house can already print to it directly.
The checks against private-network addresses in the download step are a design requirement, not an existing plugin feature.
'No destination configured' comes from the 9 Oct check and was not re-run.

sources.title: lp(1)
sources.supports: The CUPS lp command prints a file to a named printer and takes a copies count, the two options the plugin needs.

sources.title: lpadmin(8)
sources.supports: The CUPS lpadmin command creates a print queue, including a driverless IPP Everywhere queue, the one-time setup step.

sources.title: Web fetch
sources.supports: The built-in fetch tool returns readable text from a page, not the original file, so the plugin must download a PDF itself.

sources.title: iMessage media and attachments
sources.supports: Printing a file someone just texted requires inbound attachments to be switched on first.

sources.title: Command-Line Printing and Options (OpenPrinting CUPS)
sources.supports: The standard printing commands take a destination and a copy count and can list available printers.

sources.title: How to scan documents on your iPhone or iPad (Apple Support)
sources.supports: The Notes app on iPhone scans paper to a document with automatic capture and corner adjustment.

sources.title: About AirPrint (Apple Support)
sources.supports: An iPhone prints without drivers to an AirPrint-enabled printer on the same Wi-Fi network; whether this printer is one was not confirmed.

adds: States plainly that printing and scanning need no screen control: printing is one lp command once a print queue exists, scanning is the iPhone's document scanner sent as an attachment (F001, F002). Whether this printer supports AirPrint from the phones is unconfirmed.

F081.name: Scheduled home scenes and goodnight check (read-only first)
F081.description: At 22:30 a parent gets a text only if lights or speakers are still on, switching nothing; scheduled bedtime scenes come later, after a dry-run period.
F081.how: Command payload (no model) runs openhue and sonos status, printing NO_REPLY when all is off; automation approvals never reach chat and Lobster is off in sandboxes, so actuation starts dry-run.
corrections: 'Isolated runs cannot approve' is too strong: the exec approvals doc says approvals from scheduled runs are delivered to connected approval clients (Control UI, the apps) and the run waits, but they never go to chat channels and are denied at once when no such client is connected. For an iMessage-only household the conclusion is unchanged: use a dry-run period, not per-call approval.
unverified: Whether plugin-tool approvals raised inside a scheduled run follow the same delivery rule as exec approvals.
That the two CLIs report 'on' states in a form a short script can parse reliably was not tried (neither is installed).

sources.title: Automation payloads
sources.supports: A command job runs a script on the gateway host with no model call, so the nightly check costs no tokens and has no prompt to inject into.

sources.title: Exec approvals
sources.supports: Approvals raised by scheduled runs go only to connected approval clients such as the Control UI, never to chat, and are denied if none is connected.

sources.title: Lobster
sources.supports: The Lobster workflow tool is switched off in sandboxed tool contexts, so it cannot gate a sandboxed home agent.

F082.name: Structured interaction primitives: ask_user and llm-task
F082.description: Happy asks one short numbered question when a request is ambiguous, and turns newsletter or flyer text into clean event and item lists.
F082.how:
Allow ask_user for

-main only; enable bundled llm-task with tools.alsoAllow, a JSON schema, llm.allowedCompletionModels listing both custom ids, allowModelOverride false.
unverified: Whether Happy's custom OpenAI provider route runs llm-task with a truly empty tool surface; the doc carves out an 'Agents API' runtime whose service may keep built-in helpers.
That a plain iMessage reply is matched to the pending question on this install; the doc requires the replier's permissions to match the question's creator and this was not tried.

sources.title: Ask user (installed docs)
sources.anchor: available only in the main session
sources.supports: ask_user is offered only to the main session, so mail-reader and scheduled runs never get it.

sources.title: LLM task (installed docs)
sources.supports: The model allowlist applies to every llm-task completion, so the agent's default model must be on it as well as the cheap model.

sources.title: Ask user (public OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The public page states the same main-session limit and a default wait of fifteen minutes.

F083.name: home_weather v2: NWS alerts, hourly rain and snow
F083.description: Ask about rain during Saturday's game or active weather alerts for home, with hour-by-hour detail and snowfall, straight from the National Weather Service.
F083.how: Extend the in-house home_weather plugin: follow forecastHourly from /points, add alert id, read snowfallAmount from the raw gridpoint endpoint; keep the api.weather.gov host pin.
unverified: The snowfall field name and units were seen only in the OpenAPI description of the raw gridpoint endpoint, not in a live response.
NWS publishes no numeric rate limit, so the 10-minute cache is a design choice rather than an NWS rule.
That Apple Weather on each phone already pushes the same alerts and hourly rain (no Apple page was fetched for this).

sources.title: National Weather Service: API Web Service documentation
sources.supports: The points lookup hands back the hourly forecast address for a location; a User-Agent is required and the rate limit is unpublished with retry after a few seconds.

sources.title: weather.gov API: OpenAPI specification
sources.supports: Active alerts can be filtered by a latitude and longitude point; each alert carries an id, headline, severity and end time, and the raw gridpoint data lists a snowfall layer.

sources.title: Building plugins (installed docs)
sources.supports: A plugin adds its own agent tool in code, which is how the existing home_weather tool is delivered and extended.

sources.title: Tool policy (installed docs)
sources.supports: With sandbox mode set to all, a plugin's tools stay visible only if the plugin id is in the sandbox tool allowlist.

sources.title: Bundled weather skill
sources.supports: The bundled weather skill depends on web_fetch against a third-party site, which Happy does not have, so the in-house NWS plugin stays the right path.

F084.name: Local privacy gate for documents (tier-C refusal)
F084.description: Before any attachment goes to the cloud model, Happy refuses PDFs that look like bank statements or tax forms and says why.
F084.how: In-house plugin: before_agent_run returns outcome block on regex hits in the extracted file text; needs hooks.allowConversationAccess; photos cannot be checked locally yet.
unverified: That the extracted file text is inside the prompt field the hook receives; the doc only says the hook gets the current user input. Needs a test with a seeded PDF.
Which config key holds allowedMimes for iMessage attachments; the only documented allowedMimes keys sit under the Gateway HTTP API endpoints.
The exact point at which an inbound PDF falls back to page images; the 200-characters-per-page rule is documented for the pdf tool, not for channel attachments.
Photo gating is blocked, not just weak: no local vision model exists on this install, so only a caption keyword rule is possible.

sources.title: Media understanding (installed docs)
sources.supports: Every inbound document is extracted and placed in front of the model on the first turn, with no tool call a tool hook could intercept.

sources.title: Prompt and session hooks (installed docs)
sources.supports: This hook runs after the prompt is built and before the model sees it, can block the run with a replacement message, and the original text is not kept.

sources.title: Hook reference (installed docs)
sources.supports: If this hook throws or exceeds 15 seconds the run is blocked rather than allowed.

sources.title: Plugin hooks (installed docs)
sources.supports: A non-bundled plugin's before_agent_run handler only runs when the operator grants it conversation access in config.

sources.title: PDF tool (installed docs)
sources.supports: In the pdf tool, pages with little extractable text are rendered to images, which is how a scanned statement would reach a vision model unread.

sources.title: iMessage media and attachments (installed docs)
sources.supports: Inbound iMessage attachments are dropped unless the operator switches them on, so the gate matters only once that switch is flipped.

sources.title: OpenAI API guide: Your data
sources.supports: API inputs are not used for training by default but abuse-monitoring logs can keep content for up to a month, and image and file inputs get extra scanning.

F085.name: Memory hygiene, privacy controls and weekly memory review
F085.description: Mail-reader sessions stay out of long-term memory, a parent can have a session's memories removed, and each adult gets a short Sunday review of what Happy learned.
F085.how: memoryPolicy.excludeSessions.hookExternalContentSources [email, gmail]; operator runbook for openclaw memory forget --dry-run; weekly isolated automation with --tools memory_search,memory_get; openclaw memory promote --apply.
corrections: 'Forget what I said about X works' (9 Oct description) is not a platform ability: memory forget selects whole sessions by id, hook source or participant, never by topic or message text, and reworded copies are outside its cleanup. Topic-level forgetting is a hand edit of the memory file.

'Promote via openclaw memory promote --apply' will usually promote nothing a parent just confirmed: by default a candidate needs a 0.75 score, three recalls and three distinct queries. Either pass lower thresholds or write the confirmed line to MEMORY.md directly.
unverified: With dreaming switched off (roadmap decision) the session-exclusion setting has little to act on today; its effect was not tested.
The memory-wiki dashboards named on 9 Oct (privacy review, stale pages) are documented, but the plugin is not enabled on this install.

sources.title: Memory configuration reference (installed docs)
sources.supports: The exclusion list only keeps matching sessions out of dreaming ingestion and backfill; it does not erase memories or limit workspace writes.

sources.title: Memory CLI (installed docs)
sources.supports: memory forget deletes at once with no confirmation unless run as a preview, so the runbook must always preview first.

sources.title: Memory provenance and deletion (installed docs)
sources.supports: Reworded copies of a fact, exports and backups are outside what the forget command cleans.

sources.title: Automation payloads (installed docs)
sources.supports: A scheduled job can be limited to a named tool list, which keeps the weekly review run read-only.

F086.name: Apple Foundation Models as the free on-device utility model
F086.description: The Mac mini's built-in Apple model handles tiny background chores for free; the family sees no difference in iMessage.
F086.how: Bundled apple-fm plugin; openclaw onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice apple-fm --accept-risk as the happy user; utilityModel apple-fm/system; needs Swift tools and an 8,192-token model.
corrections: The catalog's command is incomplete: the documented scripted form is 'openclaw onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice apple-fm --accept-risk'.
unverified: The one use the catalog keeps (a free local classifier for F084 through llm-task) is not documented: llm-task needs a runtime that supports isolated completion and no page says apple-fm does.
Whether Apple Intelligence can be switched on and its model downloaded inside the non-admin happy account, and whether this Mac reports the 8,192-token variant; both need the on-machine probe.
Apple lists the framework from macOS 26 while OpenClaw's page requires macOS 27; only OpenClaw's own requirement was confirmed.

sources.title: Apple Foundation Models plugin (installed docs)
sources.supports: The option appears only when the Mac reports an on-device model with a large enough window; owning an Apple silicon Mac on macOS 27 is not sufficient by itself.

sources.title: Agent model configuration (installed docs)
sources.supports: The utility model only powers session titles, recaps and progress narration on surfaces Happy does not use, so the family-visible gain on iMessage is nil.

sources.title: Apple Developer Documentation: Foundation Models (page data for /documentation/foundationmodels)
sources.supports: Apple's framework exposes an on-device language model with structured output and tool calling, on devices that support Apple Intelligence.

sources.title: Apple Support: Apple Intelligence requirements (article 121115)
sources.supports: Apple Intelligence runs on M-series Macs, needs device and Siri language to match and several gigabytes of storage for the model.

F087.name: Approval-gated multi-step workflows (Lobster)
F087.description: A way to run fixed multi-step chores with an approve-to-continue pause; it amounts to host shell access, so it stays off for a family agent.
F087.how: Separately installed @openclaw/lobster plugin, tools.alsoAllow lobster; runs shell steps in the Gateway process, disabled in sandboxed contexts; before_tool_call requireApproval covers approvals instead.
unverified: No config switch that forbids model-written inline pipelines was found; the proposed hook that rejects them is untested.

sources.title: Lobster (installed docs)
sources.supports: Lobster is a separate official plugin that runs workflows inside the Gateway process and returns a resume token when a step waits for approval.

sources.title: Tool call policy hooks (installed docs)
sources.supports: A plugin hook can already pause any tool call for a human approval answered with /approve, without granting host shell.

sources.title: openclaw/lobster (GitHub repository)
sources.supports: Upstream describes Lobster as a workflow shell whose steps run operating-system commands, with approval steps that pause and resume.

F087.reject_reason: Lobster's approve-to-continue pipelines amount to host shell access inside a person's agent, and the existing approval hook already provides the gate.

G001.name: Notification policy: quiet hours, daily cap, priority classes, job tag on every proactive text
G001.description: Happy stays quiet at night, caps how many unprompted texts each parent gets a day, and labels each one so you know why it arrived.
G001.how: In-house plugin: before_tool_call on message (fail-closed) plus message_sending cancel for --announce deliveries (fail-open on error); counters in home-store; schedules generated inside allowed windows.
corrections: reply_payload_sending does not cover --announce on the installed build: the scheduler's announce path sends without a reply-payload hook descriptor and the outbound stage skips that hook when none is supplied. message_sending is the hook that sees those deliveries (the G005 wording already uses it), and it fails open on handler error, so it is a best-effort gate.
unverified: The announce-path reading comes from bundled JavaScript, not a doc page; confirm with a throwaway hook before relying on either hook.
How the hook learns which job produced a text; no doc lists a job id on message_sending, so the job may have to write its own tag into the text.
Whether a scheduled iPhone Do Not Disturb can silence only Happy's thread; Apple's page confirmed scheduling and allowed people, not per-contact silencing.

sources.title: Message and delivery hooks (installed docs)
sources.supports: A plugin can rewrite or cancel any outgoing message just before delivery.

sources.title: Hook reference (installed docs)
sources.anchor: Log and skip the failed handler
sources.supports: Outbound delivery hooks are not hard gates: if the handler throws or times out the message is still sent.

sources.title: Outbound delivery preparation (installed source)
sources.supports: The shared outbound stage runs the reply-payload hook only when the caller passes a hook descriptor, while message_sending runs whenever a handler is registered.

sources.title: Scheduler announce delivery (installed source)
sources.supports: Scheduled announce deliveries are sent through the durable batch call without a reply-payload hook descriptor.

sources.title: Control UI notifications (installed docs)
sources.supports: The only built-in quiet hours belong to Control UI browser and app notifications, not to chat channels.

sources.title: Prompt and session hooks (installed docs)
sources.supports: The scheduled job id is available to some agent hooks but not to before_tool_call, so the job tag needs another source.

sources.title: Apple Support: Do Not Disturb on iPhone or iPad (article 105112)
sources.supports: Each iPhone can already silence notifications on a schedule while allowing chosen people, so the plugin's distinct value is the daily cap and batching.

G002.name: Snooze, mute and vacation mode by chat
G002.description: Either parent texts 'mute until 3' or 'we are away next week' and briefs, bin reminders and routines pause for that window while urgent alerts still arrive.
G002.how: Paused-until row in the planned home-store plugin that each job reads first, answering `NO_REPLY`; or `openclaw automations disable|enable <job-id>` from a host helper; `cron.enabled: false` pauses everything.
corrections:
The 9 Oct note said switching jobs off needs operator.admin and so cannot be done from

-main; the installed docs also let a sender listed in `commands.ownerAllowFrom` ask the agent to disable an existing automation by chat.
unverified: The home-store plugin does not exist yet; the paused-until row is a design, not an installed feature.
Keeping 'urgent classes' on during a mute depends on the planned notification-policy plugin (G001); no built-in quiet hours or priority classes were found.
Switching the brief to trip context (destination weather) is a prompt idea with no source.

sources.title: CLI reference: silent token suppression
sources.supports: A job that answers only the silent token sends nothing, which is how a paused window is honoured per job.

sources.title: Managing automations
sources.supports: A job can be switched off without deleting it.

sources.title: Configuration: automations (cron)
sources.supports: One config switch pauses every stored job without deleting any, a whole-house vacation fallback.

G003.name: Jobs registry and per-feature flags in family.json5
G003.description: Every scheduled feature becomes a named switch per person in one file, so turning Jordan's school digest off is a one-line change Tony can review.

corrections: Diffing against 'automations list --json' is not enough: the list shows enabled jobs only unless --all is passed, so a job disabled by a mute would look missing and be created twice. Use 'automations list --all --json'.

G007.name: Nightly backups and a quarterly restore drill
G007.description: Happy's memory, settings and history are copied every night to an encrypted place off the Mac's main disk, and a quarterly test proves the copy restores.
G007.how: openclaw backup create --verify nightly via launchd or a command automation, encrypted with age; openclaw backup restore --target for the drill; separate tar for home-store and family.json5.
corrections: 'backup sqlite create --repository' alone is not a valid call and is not Git-versioned: it needs exactly one source (--global or --agent <id>) and writes plain snapshot directories. Git history is the separate 'openclaw backup git' command family.

Scheduling is not wholly outside the tool: 'openclaw backup enable --repository <dir> --every 24h' creates a nightly Git backup job. Only the archive and plain SQLite snapshot routes leave scheduling, rotation and encryption to the operator.

Secrets are not excluded by default (9 Oct 'needs' said they stay in Keychain): the full archive covers auth profiles and channel/provider credentials; only resolved secrets in the config copy are left out, and a secrets-excluding switch exists only for Git backups.
unverified: Whether a later memory-wiki vault is picked up as a plugin-declared backup resource or needs its own tar step.
The quarterly canary (answering a question from the restored copy) has no documented one-command path; activating restored state is an offline operator step.

G009.name: Family delivery primitive: message an allowlisted family member or the group chat, recipient-pinned
G009.description: Happy can pass a short text from one parent to the other or to the parents' group, and can never message anyone outside the family.
G009.how:
message tool on

-main with a before_tool_call plugin hook that blocks any target not in family.json5 (fails closed); host jobs use openclaw agent --deliver or openclaw message send.
corrections: Markdown adds message_sending 'as a second gate'. That hook can cancel a send, but when its handler throws or times out it is logged and skipped (hooks/reference.md:94), so it fails open; only the before_tool_call check is fail-closed.

The 9 Oct 'needs' implies that enabling the tool plus the hook is enough. The live config turns both crossContext switches off, and tool-permissions.md:39 says that confines sends to the current conversation, so the same-provider switch must be re-opened and the hook then becomes the only recipient limit.
unverified: The exact parameter that carries the recipient in a message tool call, which the hook must match, was not read from source.
openclaw message send takes no agent flag and runs as the configured System Agent (cli/message.md:35-50); whether that suits per-person jobs was not tested.
The hook plugin and its family-only test case do not exist yet, so blocking an unknown recipient is unproven on this install.

G015.name:
Per-person mail reader agent (

-mail): isolated, memory-off, no web, deliver-to-owner only
G015.description: One locked-down mail agent per adult: it can read that adult's mail and write drafts, cannot browse or run code, and can only message its owner.
G015.how:
Agent entry with `profile: "minimal"`, explicit `

-gmail__*` allow plus the `tools.sandbox.tools` gate, deny web/fs/runtime/browser, owner-pinned send hook; checked with `openclaw sandbox explain --agent`.
corrections: The 9 Oct needs list omits the sandbox-layer gate: with sandbox mode 'all', MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130). The minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly either (same file, lines 36 and 41).

'Memory off' is not one switch in the installed docs: memory search has a per-agent override (`agents.entries.*.memory.search`, `enabled`, docs/reference/memory-config.md:31 and :102), dreaming is plugin-wide (docs/concepts/memory.md:275), and `excludeSessions.hookExternalContentSources` only matches hook sessions (docs/reference/memory-config.md:667).

'Send pinned to owner' only applies when the mail agent runs its own scheduled or hook turn: when spawned from `

-main` it always loses `message` and `session_status` (docs/tools/subagents/tool-policy.md:23), so its allow list must not consist of `session_status` alone.
The 9 Oct needs list puts `openclaw models status --agent --probe` in the deploy checks; the installed doc says a direct probe needs the Gateway stopped (docs/cli/models.md:121).
unverified: The per-person provider setting that sends store false was verified in M1 and not re-read here.
Whether this OpenAI account has zero retention; without it the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to mail text sent to the model.
The promptfoo boundary canary is in-house.
A before_tool_call hook reaching MCP tool calls is implied by the doc ('every tool call in the run', docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md:222) but I found no sentence naming MCP tools.

AUT-01.name: Multi-day family project with check-ins
AUT-01.description: A parent hands Happy a project with an end date (birthday party, weekend trip, garage clean-out). Happy keeps one project note with decisions and open items, checks in on a schedule it paces itself, runs research legs in the background, and stops when the date passes. New against the 9 Oct catalog: durable project state plus paced check-ins; F028 only covers a one-shot plan.
AUT-01.example: Plan our 10-year-old's birthday party for Saturday the 14th: 10 kids, indoor, under 300 dollars. Check in with me every few days until it is sorted.
AUT-01.how:
Held by the asking parent's

-main. State: one project note (memory/projects/.md through the F041 write path, or home-store rows from F031) with goal, end date, decisions, open items and a review date. The note records only what the parent typed or confirmed, written in a turn that carried no web or research results. Check-ins: one isolated automation per project, created through the `automations` tool on

-main with a `pacing` object (`min`, `max`; `--pacing-min` and `--pacing-max` are the CLI spelling), so each run can call `automations(action: "next_check")` and be clamped to those bounds. The job's tool cap holds the note or home-store read tools plus `automations` (inside an automation run that tool is limited to the run's own job) and never `sessions_spawn` or a web tool; announce to the owner; NO_REPLY when nothing is due; the run removes its own job after the end date. Hard prerequisites before `automations` is allowed on

-main: the fail-closed before_tool_call pin must also match `automations`/`cron` add and update and refuse webhook delivery, completion and failure destinations, and any recipient other than the asking parent; and `cron.triggers.enabled: false`, so the tool does not offer script payloads, trigger scripts or stream commands. Research legs: `sessions_spawn` to the stateless `research` agent with `runTimeoutSeconds` and `completionTarget: "parent"`, in interactive turns only, so

-main reviews the result privately before it texts anything. Decisions are plain proposals in chat (or `ask_user` while the parent is in the conversation). `/goal` is not the durable state here (see AUT-02).
depends_on: F041 memory write path or F031 home-store
decision: Jordan as a command owner
delivery pin hook that covers automations/cron add and update (extends G009 and F007)
caveats: Scheduled runs do not get MEMORY.md injected, so a check-in must read the project note with a tool or carry the state in the job message.
A job created from chat is capped to the tools the creating turn had and cannot be widened later, so a check-in can never do more than the parent's own main agent.
The conversation resets every morning at 04:00 and that also wipes any /goal; the project note is the only continuity between days.
Every check-in is a cloud model turn. Pace in days, not minutes, and cap active projects per person (three is plenty).

Published measurements put the reliable autonomous working span of frontier models at well under a working day, so the design is many short runs with a parent between them, not one long unattended run.
No bookings, purchases or invitations sent: the output is options, links and drafts. A static checklist is still easier in a shared Notes or Reminders list; Happy adds the nudging and the research.

The one long-task measurement opened in this run dates from March 2025 and covers software tasks: the frontier model of that time finished about half of the tasks that take a person roughly 50 minutes. It says nothing direct about gpt-6-sol or about family planning. The case for many short runs with a parent between them rests on cost and on keeping a person in the loop, not on that number.

Command-owner status is gateway-wide: an owner can ask their agent to list, inspect, update, run or remove any job on the gateway, whoever created it. Once Jordan is an owner, each parent's agent can read and change the other's check-in jobs, so job messages must not carry private detail.

The F041 plan refuses memory writes in a turn tainted by web results, and a turn that received a research result is tainted. Research findings therefore cannot be saved into the project note in that turn: they stay in the chat thread, and the note holds only what the parent states or confirms afterwards.
AUT-01.safety:
-main holds the note and never browses; `research` does every web leg, has no memory, and as a sub-agent can never get the message, cron or gateway tools. The `automations` tool is itself a send path: a job can name any chat as its delivery target or post its result to a webhook URL.

-main holds memory and reads search snippets, so the recipient pin must cover `automations`/`cron` calls, not only `message`, and must refuse webhook mode before the tool is granted. Check-in runs carry no web tool and no `sessions_spawn`; that is the hard limit. The rule that handoff text carries dates, ages and budget only (never names, school or address) is prompt text, not enforcement. With the pin in place nothing on the never list is reachable: there is no payment, booking or outbound-to-strangers tool anywhere in the chain.
unverified: Whether a custom-session job (`--session session:<id>`) is exempt from the daily reset policy, which would let check-ins keep conversational context.
Whether memory read tools can be named in a job tool cap for a sandboxed agent on 2026.9.7; test at build time.
That research handoffs return results with agent-to-agent off and session visibility self (already an open item in the roadmap).
Whether the gateway accepts webhook delivery or an arbitrary recipient on a job that an agent creates from an iMessage owner turn. The tool description offers both; it was not tested.
Whether next_check and self-removal stay callable when the job's tool cap leaves out `automations`.
Whether the F041 path hook, written for memory/*.md, admits a memory/projects/ subfolder.

AUT-02.name: Session goal (/goal) for same-day focus
AUT-02.description: One pinned objective per conversation that Happy is reminded of on every turn until it is done, paused or cleared. Fine for a long same-day working session; on this stack it is not a multi-day tracker, because the goal does not survive the nightly session reset.
AUT-02.example: /goal finish the camp registration today: forms, immunization record, payment reminder
AUT-02.how:
`/goal start|edit|pause|resume|complete|clear` typed in the parent's own DM with

-main; state lives on that session entry. For the model to read the goal or mark it complete or blocked, add `get_goal`, `create_goal` and `update_goal` to that agent's `tools.alsoAllow` and to `tools.sandbox.tools.allow` (they ship in the `coding` profile and `group:agents`, not in `minimal`). No plugin, no account.
depends_on: none; pairs with AUT-01 for anything longer than a day
caveats: The installed build clears the goal whenever a new session starts, and Happy starts a new session at the first message after 04:00 every day. The docs mention only /new and /reset; the compiled source clears it on every rollover.
One goal per session; a second one is refused until the first is cleared.
A goal does not schedule, deliver or approve anything, so it produces no check-ins by itself.
The token budget is a per-goal guardrail, not a spend cap.
Built for coding sessions (the documented examples are pull-request closeouts); the status pill exists only in the Control UI and TUI, not in iMessage.
AUT-02.safety: Adds no tool reach and no outbound path. The objective is typed by the parent and injected as user-role context; the model cannot pause, clear or replace it, only report complete or blocked.
unverified: Whether `/goal` text commands are accepted from an allowlisted non-owner iMessage sender on 2026.9.7.
Whether a `session.resetByType` override for direct chats would keep goals alive without bringing back the cost problem the daily reset was added to fix.

AUT-03.name: Self-paced watch loop (/loop and paced automations)
AUT-03.description: "Keep checking this until it happens, then tell me": a recurring agent turn bound to the conversation, at a fixed interval or self-paced so it checks more often while things move and backs off when quiet.
AUT-03.example: /loop 30m has the district posted a decision about tomorrow's snow day? Stop once it is posted.
AUT-03.how:
`/loop [interval] ` typed to

-main makes the agent create a recurring agent-turn job in that conversation through the `automations` tool; with no interval it self-paces between 1 minute and 1 hour using `next_check`. `/loop status` and `/loop stop` manage it. Longer-lived watchers are created by happy-deploy with `openclaw automations add --pacing-min ... --pacing-max ...` and an explicit `--tools` cap. Needs `automations` allowed on

-main (it is denied today with the rest of `group:automation`).
depends_on: decision: Jordan as a command owner
F029 for anything that needs page content
delivery pin hook that covers automations/cron add and update (extends G009 and F007)
caveats: Owner-only: Jordan cannot use /loop unless she is listed as a command owner, which is a gateway-wide elevation. An owner can list, inspect, update, run or remove every job on the gateway, including the other parent's.
Every tick is a cloud model turn and the self-paced floor is one minute. Require an explicit interval of 15 minutes or more and a stop condition, in AGENTS.md.

-main has web_search only, so a loop sees search snippets, not page content. Whether a change posted minutes ago shows up in snippets within the loop interval is untested, so the snow-day example is not dependable this way. Real page watching belongs to the research agent (F029).
A loop does not end by itself. The scheduler disables a recurring job only after 10 failures in a row, so the prompt must say when to stop.
Nothing fires while the Mac is off or locked after a reboot.
For known sources the phone is already better: district push alerts, carrier tracking, calendar alerts.
AUT-03.safety:
Inside a loop run the `automations` tool is limited to the run's own job, and the result returns to the conversation that created it. The exposure comes from granting `automations` to

-main at all: in an interactive owner turn the tool can create a job whose delivery names any chat or a webhook URL and, unless `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, script payloads, trigger scripts and stream commands.

-main holds memory and reads untrusted search snippets, so without a fail-closed before_tool_call pin on `automations`/`cron` that refuses webhook mode and any recipient but the asker, the tool completes the trifecta. With the pin in place and triggers off, what remains is the exposure

-main already has with web_search, now repeated unattended. Keep loops short-lived, count them against the G001 daily cap, and never give a looped agent web_fetch.
unverified: Whether a conversation-bound loop keeps running, or is orphaned, across the 04:00 session rollover.
The exact tool cap a /loop job records under the minimal profile on this config.
Whether the gateway accepts webhook delivery or an arbitrary recipient on a job that an agent creates from an iMessage owner turn. The tool description offers both; it was not tested.
How quickly the search index reflects a newly posted page (not measured).

AUT-04.name: Standing orders: a written charter per recurring job
AUT-04.description: Each recurring family job gets a short charter in the agent's AGENTS.md: what Happy may do without asking, when it runs, what needs a yes first, when to stop and ask, and what it must never do. Parents can read it and changes go through the config repo. New against the catalog: G003 registers the jobs, but nothing states their authority in one reviewable place.
AUT-04.example: Job message at 19:30: "Run the evening brief per standing orders." Parent text: "From now on don't text me about bins when I'm travelling" becomes a line under that program's What NOT to do at the next deploy.
AUT-04.how:
`## Program: ` sections (Authority, Trigger, Approval gate, Escalation, What NOT to do, plus an execute-verify-report rule) in templates/person/AGENTS.md, rendered per person by gen-family from the same family.json5 entries that drive the G003 job registry. Each automation message points at its program instead of repeating it. Isolated jobs must not use `--light-context`, which skips the bootstrap files. Held by each

-main, and by each reader agent for its own program.
caveats: A charter is prompt text, not enforcement. It survives compaction because AGENTS.md is re-injected, but an injected page can still argue with it; the hard limits stay in tool policy and hooks.
AGENTS.md shares a bootstrap budget (20,000 characters per file by default). Keep each program to about ten lines.
Sub-agents get AGENTS.md only, and scheduled runs do not get MEMORY.md, so anything a program needs must be in AGENTS.md, the job message, or a tool result.
The documented examples are business programs (posting content, restarting services, sending reports to stakeholders). Family programs are read-and-notify only; do not copy those authorities.
A chat instruction does not change the charter: config writes from chat are off and the agents have no file tools, so it waits for a deploy.
AUT-04.safety: Charters narrow behaviour and grant nothing. Never-list items are written under What NOT to do and are also unreachable by tool policy. No change to which agent holds private data, reads untrusted content, or can send.

AUT-06.name: Teach Happy a routine (operator-reviewed skills)
AUT-06.description: A parent describes once how the family does something; it becomes a named skill Happy follows every time (party plan, ski-trip packing, school-form explainer). A skill goes live only after Tony has read it.
AUT-06.example: Happy, learn our ski-trip packing routine: ask how many nights and who is coming, then list by person, and always include the kids' helmets.
AUT-06.how:
Happy answers with the drafted procedure as plain text (no tool needed). Tony turns it into `skills//SKILL.md` (a `name` and a one-line `description`, optionally `user-invocable`) in happy-config under that person's template, reviews it, and happy-deploy copies it into that agent's workspace `skills/` folder, the highest-precedence skill root. To use a skill the model must load its SKILL.md with the `read` tool; the system prompt lists only each skill's name, description and location. So

-main needs `read` in `tools.alsoAllow` and in the sandbox tool allowlist (group:fs is denied today). With `workspaceAccess: "none"` OpenClaw mirrors eligible skills into the sandbox workspace as read-only copies and `read` is rooted there. Keep `skill_workshop` denied on every family agent. Alternative for agent-scoped Workshop skills: `openclaw skills workshop propose-create --agent

-main --proposal ./PROPOSAL.md`, then inspect and apply, run as the happy user from the deploy path. Per-agent visibility through `agents.entries..skills`; inbox keeps `skills: []`. Held by the asking parent's

-main; shared stateless agents get only skills meant for everyone. A routine of a few lines can instead live as a section of AGENTS.md, which needs no tool.
depends_on: a skills step in happy-deploy and gen-family
decision: who may request a new skill

`read` allowed on

-main in tools.alsoAllow and the sandbox tool allowlist (group:fs is denied today; arrives with F041)
caveats: Asking Happy to save a skill from iMessage does not work on this stack by default: sandboxed runs do not construct the `skill_workshop` tool even when it is allowlisted, so `/learn` cannot stage a draft. The M1 doctor baseline in the config repo already shows this warning for every agent. The documented exception is a human turn with host-granted library-authoring authority, and personal-library authoring publishes with no pending draft, which would skip Tony's review. That is one more reason to keep `skill_workshop` off every family agent's allowlist.
A skill is know-how. It cannot add tools or accounts, so "learn to order the groceries" still ends at a list.
A skill is instruction text loaded into future sessions. One written from a pasted web page or an email is a stored injection, so author only from the parent's own words.
No marketplace skills: an audit reported by The Hacker News found 341 malicious entries among 2,857 ClawHub skills in early 2026.
A running session keeps the skill list it started with; a new skill appears after /new or the next morning's reset.
Turnaround is "when Tony next deploys", not instant.
A new or changed workspace skill is picked up on the next turn after the skills watcher sees the file change, or after the gateway restart that a deploy performs. No /new is needed.
AUT-06.safety:
Operator review is the gate: no model-written file ever reaches a skills root. A skill cannot widen tool policy, so the trifecta split between

-main, research and the mail readers is unchanged. Per-person skills live in that person's workspace, so nothing crosses data domains.
unverified: Whether a user-invocable skill command typed by an allowlisted non-owner iMessage sender is accepted on 2026.9.7.
That skill sync into the sandbox works with `workspaceAccess: "none"` (the docs say sandboxed runs read materialized copies).

That a `read`-only grant on a sandboxed

-main reaches the mirrored skills and nothing private; check at build time.
Whether an iMessage owner turn is ever given library-authoring authority on this configuration. If it is, an allowlisted `skill_workshop` could publish a skill with no review.

AUT-07.name: Automatic self-learning: switch it off explicitly
AUT-07.description: OpenClaw can review finished conversations on its own and write or edit skills in the background. For a family agent this stays off; skills arrive only through AUT-06. The default is on, and Happy's config does not set it yet.
AUT-07.example: A parent asks: "Can Happy just learn from our chats?" Trigger if left on: about 30 seconds after a long turn, a background review of that conversation starts.
AUT-07.how: Add `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "off"` to happy-config (the default is `auto`) and `skills.workshop.approvalPolicy: "pending"` for any later proposal flow. After the deploy, check `openclaw cron list --all` for the weekly Skill Workshop review row, and expect doctor's `core/doctor/skill-workshop-tool-policy` warnings to disappear. Gateway-wide setting; no agent holds anything new.
caveats: In auto mode the background reviewer edits skill files with ordinary file tools: no proposal, no scanner pass and no rollback snapshot.
A review re-sends the conversation, tool inputs and results included, to the model provider: extra cost and another copy of private chat in a provider call.
Auto mode also enables a weekly collection-review job on the agent's own model.

On Happy today the reviews most likely fail closed, because every agent is sandboxed and the authoring tool is not constructed. So the default currently buys doctor warnings, not learning; the explicit setting makes that intentional and upgrade-proof.
Propose mode is the only variant worth revisiting, and it still needs a non-sandboxed session to stage a draft.

Off stops autonomous capture only. `/learn` and explicit Workshop requests stay available in every mode; on Happy they are stopped by the sandbox gate and by `skill_workshop` not being on any allowlist, so both of those must stay as they are.
AUT-07.safety: Skills are instructions loaded into later sessions. Letting a model write them from conversations that include web search results is a path from untrusted content to persistent behaviour with no human in between, which is the kind of control the roadmap rules out. Off is a hard stop for background capture. It does not cover a skill requested in chat (`/learn`); on Happy that path is closed by the sandbox gate and by keeping `skill_workshop` off every allowlist.

AUT-08.name: Unattended-job guardrails (failure alerts, auto-disable, missed runs)
AUT-08.description: Rules that stop scheduled family jobs from failing silently or misfiring after an outage: failures alert Tony rather than the family, a job that keeps failing stops itself, stale runs are skipped after a power cut, and every job has a time limit and a tool cap. New against the catalog: the built-in scheduler behaviour and defaults that G003 and G008 should be built on.
AUT-08.example: The 19:30 brief fails twice in a row: Tony gets one text, and one more when it recovers. After a power cut, the 07:00 brief does not turn up at 11:40.
AUT-08.how: In happy-config: a global `cron.failureAlert` object routed to the operator's handle, so alerts do not fall back to each job's own announce target; `--timeout-seconds` and an explicit `--tools` cap on every job the G003 registry emits; `cron.skipMissedJobs: true` for recurring jobs; `cron.triggers.enabled: false`, set before any agent is given the `automations` tool and kept until F029 deliberately turns triggers back on. happy-inspect reads `openclaw automations list --all` to catch auto-disabled jobs. The healthchecks dead-man switch stays as the only signal for a Mac that is off. Gateway-level; no agent gains anything.
caveats: By default a failure alert goes to the failing job's own announce target, so Jordan would receive "job failed" texts for her jobs unless they are rerouted.
Alerts start after 2 failures in a row with a 1-hour cooldown; repeats with the same cause count as one incident and one recovery notice closes it.
A recurring job is switched off after 10 failures in a row and then disappears from the default job list.
Without a per-job timeout an isolated agent job is bounded only by a 60-minute watchdog.
Jobs run inside the gateway. After a reboot with FileVault locked nothing fires and nothing alerts, and by default the scheduler catches up on missed recurring runs later.
One-shot reminders still catch up after an outage even with skipMissedJobs set; a late reminder is sometimes worse than none.

Once

-main has the automations tool, the agent offers to turn a repeated request into a schedule and creates it enabled with an immediate test run. That is pleasant, but those jobs are not in the G003 registry, so the registry diff must tolerate or report them.

Trigger scripts and script payloads run with the owning agent's full tool policy, exec included, in the Code Mode executor, and the docs name `cron.triggers.enabled` as their only switch. With triggers on, the `automations` tool also offers the model script payloads, trigger scripts and stream commands. Set `cron.triggers.enabled: false` before any agent is given that tool (F007, AUT-01, AUT-03). This switches off the trigger-script design of F029 until triggers are deliberately turned back on.
AUT-08.safety: Purely restrictive. Alert text shown in chat is a normalized cause (raw errors stay in run history), and routing alerts to the operator keeps one person's job details out of another person's thread.
unverified: The exact shape of the global `cron.failureAlert` object beyond the documented destination fields; validate in staging.
Whether scheduler-sent failure alerts pass through the G009 recipient-pin hook or bypass it.

Where the auto-disable notice lands. The docs say the owning agent receives it and that it stays active even when failure alerts are off, so it may reach the family member's thread instead of the operator's.

AUT-09.name: Happy scorecard (personal-agent benchmark themes)
AUT-09.description: A small fixed test set that scores Happy on the ten behaviours OpenClaw's own personal-agent pack checks (reminder round trip, preference recall, no secret echo, stopping after a denied approval, no fake "done", honest partial-failure reports), run against the eval clones after each change. The shipped pack itself cannot run on this install.
AUT-09.example: Tony runs `happy-eval scorecard` after a deploy and reads a ten-line pass or fail table before texting the family that something new is on.
AUT-09.how:
The shipped pack is out of reach: it needs an OpenClaw source checkout and `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1`, drives the synthetic qa-channel with a mock model, and the Homebrew npm install has no qa directory. Build instead: write the ten scenario themes as promptfoo cases in happy-config/evals against the `

-main-eval` clones through promptfoo's `openclaw` provider (the roadmap E0 harness), with fixtures standing in for reminders and approvals, and store the pass rate next to the smoke results. Operator tooling only.
depends_on: F007 and F041, so the reminder and memory cases have something to test
caveats: The upstream pack with a mock model measures the plumbing; a promptfoo port measures the real model and costs tokens on every run.
Ten cases is a regression tripwire, not a benchmark. Anthropic's guidance is to start from 20 to 50 tasks drawn from real failures and to read the transcripts, not only the scores.
Eval clones must keep messaging tools denied, or a reminder test texts the family.
The docs say not to point the upstream pack at live chat services or real accounts.

Several of the ten themes have nothing to exercise on Happy today: no tool is approval-gated, so there is nothing to deny; reminders need F007; preference recall needs F041; thread routing and diagnostics artifacts are developer-surface checks. Start with the themes that apply now (no secret echo, no fake "done", honest partial failure, pending versus done) and add the rest as the tools land.
AUT-09.safety: Runs only against eval clones with fake users and fake secrets; no live channel, no real memory, no accounts.
unverified: That the scenario YAML files are readable in the upstream repository at the 2026.9.7 tag (not fetched).
How promptfoo's tool-trajectory assertions behave against 2026.9.7 (an open item in the roadmap).

AUT-11.name: Model-written code and large fan-out (Code Mode, Swarm, remote code execution): keep off
AUT-11.description: Three platform features let the model write and run code or launch dozens of sub-agents at once. None earns a place in a family agent: two are already switched off in Happy's config and the third needs a cloud provider Happy does not use.
AUT-11.example: "Research 30 summer camps at once and make me a spreadsheet." Happy does three to five with ordinary background research and says so.
AUT-11.how:
Keep `tools.codeMode: false` and `tools.swarm: false` (both already set in happy-config), leave `plugins.entries.xai.config.codeExecution` unset, and add `cron.triggers.enabled: false`: script payloads and trigger scripts run in the same Code Mode executor, are available by default, and the docs name the triggers switch as their only control. For side-by-side comparisons,

-main starts a handful of ordinary `research` children with `sessions_spawn`: `maxSpawnDepth: 1` is already set, `maxChildrenPerAgent` defaults to 5, and `agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent` can drop from its default of 8 to 3.
depends_on: F019 research agent (for the ordinary sub-agent alternative)
caveats: Code Mode is documented as experimental. Its default executor is Node's vm module, which the docs say is not a security boundary and which shares the gateway process's privileges.
If the Code Mode key is ever absent the default is automatic activation for preferred models, so the explicit false must survive every config refactor and upgrade.
Swarm is on by default with limits sized for engineering teams (32 children at once, up to 200 per group) and is meant for five or more similar children; each child is a paid model stream.
Swarm's script interface only exists with Code Mode on.

`code_execution` runs Python on xAI's servers at 5 dollars per 1,000 calls plus tokens and needs an xAI key: a second cloud provider outside the per-person no-retention setup, for arithmetic the model can already do.
Sub-agent caps apply per spawning session, not across the whole gateway.
AUT-11.safety: Model-written JavaScript in the gateway process runs outside the Colima sandbox, beside the secret resolver and every agent's state; an injected page would become code. Off is a limit the model cannot talk past. Low fan-out caps bound cost and keep each research child reviewable.
unverified: Whether trigger scripts and script payloads, which the docs say use the same executor, still run with `tools.codeMode: false`; this matters for F029.
Not tested on Happy that a script payload or trigger script actually runs with `tools.codeMode: false`; the docs say they are available by default and name only `cron.triggers.enabled` as the switch.
Whether F029's trigger-script watcher can be kept by enabling triggers for one agent only; the documented switch is gateway-wide.

AUT-12.name: Ambient heartbeat monitor: keep off
AUT-12.description: Heartbeat wakes each agent's main session every 30 minutes so the model can "notice things". Happy has it disabled. Keep it that way and express every recurring need as its own named job.
AUT-12.example: "Can Happy just keep an eye on things and ping me if something is up?" The honest answer is a list of named watchers (weather F018, school mail F055), not a heartbeat.
AUT-12.how: `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: "0m"` (already set). If it is ever trialled: one agent only, with `isolatedSession: true`, `lightContext: true`, `activeHours`, and `target: "none"`, and a short checklist in the monitor scratch.
caveats: The default interval is 30 minutes: up to 48 cloud turns per agent per day, in the main session with its conversation history unless an isolated session is forced.
Alerts go to the owner's direct message by default, so a heartbeat on jordan-main would report to Tony's thread.

With an empty checklist it has nothing to check, and the tools it would need (calendar, mail) are deliberately not on

-main.
Setting 0m stops only the recurring cadence; event-driven wakes still exist, which is harmless here because exec is denied.
The older feature that inferred follow-ups from conversation and delivered them through heartbeat was removed in v2026.8.1, so heartbeat no longer notices promises by itself.
AUT-12.safety: Unattended main-session turns on a memory-holding agent, with a default recipient who may be a different person, cut across the one-domain-per-person rule. Named jobs with explicit owners, tool caps and recipients do the same work inside the rules.

AUT-13.name: Nightly dreaming (automatic memory consolidation): keep off, promote by hand
AUT-13.description: Dreaming would sweep every agent's recent conversations at 03:00 and promote the strongest snippets into MEMORY.md using a model call. It is gateway-wide, so it cannot be on for Tony and off for Jordan. Keep it off and use the manual preview command inside the weekly review.
AUT-13.example: Once a week Tony runs the promote preview for each adult's agent and applies only what that adult agrees to keep (F085).
AUT-13.how:
`plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.enabled: false` (already set). Manual path: `openclaw memory promote --agent

-main` to preview, `openclaw memory promote-explain --agent

-main` for one candidate, then `--apply`. The CLI has to run as the happy user. The preview is read-only, but `--apply` writes that person's MEMORY.md, so it needs a step in the deploy path or its own narrow sudo rule; the current rule covers only the deploy script and read-only commands. Gateway-wide setting; the memory belongs to each

-main.
depends_on: F041 (there must be memory worth promoting)
caveats: Dreaming is on by default in OpenClaw, so the explicit false has to survive every upgrade and config refactor.
One managed job sweeps all agent workspaces. Choosing the system agent picks who runs it and does not limit whose memory is swept.

Promotion rewrites MEMORY.md with nobody looking first. The previous file is kept in plugin state and the change is summarised in DREAMS.md in the agent's workspace (also shown in the Control UI), but no family member sees either from iMessage.

The built-in guards are real (candidates with untrusted or system provenance are dropped, and only interactive sessions are ingested), but assistant text that quotes a search result is still conversation text.
It does nothing useful until the F041 memory path exists.
AUT-13.safety: As documented, the sweep crosses the one-data-domain-per-person line: one job, one execution owner, every workspace. Automatic memory writes from sessions that included untrusted search content also remove the human gate the catalog's memory-write hook is there to keep. Manual promotion keeps that gate.
unverified: Which model key and auth profile each workspace's consolidation call uses in a multi-agent fleet.
Whether `openclaw memory promote` takes an agent selector on 2026.9.7.

AUT-14.name: Deep recall of earlier conversations (Active Memory)
AUT-14.description: When a parent asks about something from an earlier day, a short blocking recall step searches that same agent's own past private conversations and gives the answer a small summary to work from. It earns its keep on this stack because the conversation resets every morning.
AUT-14.example: What did we decide about the summer camp deposit last week?
AUT-14.how:
Per agent: `agents.entries.

-main.memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations: true` with the active-memory plugin enabled in its default `escalate` mode, which runs the recall sub-agent only when the message asks about the past and the cheap deterministic lookup found nothing strong. Direct chats only, same agent only. Held by each

-main; never on research, the readers, or inbox.
depends_on:
F041 memory path and memory tools on

-main
a check that the keyword-only memory provider supports transcript recall
decision: index session transcripts or not
a staging test that a pre-reset transcript of the same DM is recalled
caveats: It defaults to off on Happy because per-sender DM isolation is configured; it must be set explicitly per agent.
It adds a blocking model call to the replies it runs on: slower answers and extra cost.
It does not run for scheduled jobs, heartbeat or sub-agents, so the briefs get nothing from it.
Recalled excerpts come from transcripts that include search-tool output, and hidden personalization can surprise ("how did it know that").
A cheaper first step is already in the catalog: the session-memory hook plus memory search from F041. Try that before this.

Each parent has one private conversation with their agent (the iMessage DM). Recall reads the same agent's other private conversations and excludes the one being answered. Whether the pre-reset transcript of that same DM counts as another conversation is not documented; if it does not, this feature returns nothing on Happy. Test that before anything else.
AUT-14.safety: Recall stays inside one agent, which is one person: another agent's transcripts are never eligible and groups are excluded. The recall sub-agent can call only memory recall tools and nothing leaves the gateway beyond the model call the agent already makes. Treat recalled text as possibly tainted by earlier search results and keep the F041 rule that tainted turns cannot write memory.
unverified: Whether protected transcript recall works with `memory.search.provider: "none"` (keyword only, no embeddings).
Whether yesterday's pre-reset transcript of the same DM counts as another private conversation for recall.
The added latency and cost per recall on the models Happy uses.

AUT-15.name: Screen journal (Logbook): not for a family
AUT-15.description: Logbook screenshots a paired Mac every 30 seconds and has a vision model write a timeline of what was on screen. It was built for a developer's own work log. Pointed at a family computer it is surveillance that ships screenshots to a cloud model.
AUT-15.example: "Can Happy tell me what the kids did on the Mac today?" No. Use Screen Time.
AUT-15.how: It would need a paired node exposing `screen.snapshot` or `logbook.snapshot` (none is paired), the Codex plugin signed in with an OpenAI login, and `plugins.entries.logbook` enabled. Leave the plugin disabled, and if a node is ever paired for another feature, put `screen.snapshot` in `gateway.nodes.commands.deny`.

Sampled screenshots go to the configured vision model. That route needs the Codex plugin's own OpenAI sign-in, a different auth path from Happy's per-person no-retention providers.
The docs say plainly that snapshots can contain anything on screen, including secrets.
A child's screen sent to a cloud model is on the never list.
Apple's Screen Time already gives parents usage reports, app limits and schedules without screenshots.
The Mac mini's own desktop under the happy user has nothing worth journaling.

AUT-16.name: Developer, team and enterprise platform features (cloud workers, ACP harnesses, Session Share, Team Reports, Vault): skip
AUT-16.description: Cloud workers, session hosting on other machines, external coding harnesses, Session Share, Team Reports and HashiCorp Vault are built for development teams. None fits a one-Mac family agent, and two are blocked outright by Happy's own rules.
AUT-16.example: "Could Happy rent a cloud machine for a big job?" or "Can Jordan see my Happy chats?" No to both.
AUT-16.how: Leave `cloudWorkers.profiles` empty, do not install the acpx or team-reports packages, and do not enable `session-share` or `vault`. Secrets stay on the Keychain exec SecretRef chosen in M0. The 1Password plugin is the only item worth a second look, and only if the family already pays for 1Password and Tony wants to retire the Keychain script.
caveats: Cloud workers: the rented machine dials the gateway's public TLS endpoint and dispatch refuses loopback addresses, so they need exactly the public exposure the Tailscale-only rule forbids. They exist to move coding work off the host.

ACP: runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and similar harnesses. It is hidden while the requester is sandboxed, which every Happy agent is, and the roadmap forbids the happy user from signing in to Claude Code.
Session Share: read-only sharing of sessions between two gateways for teammates. Happy has one gateway, and showing one parent's transcripts to the other contradicts one data domain per person.
Team Reports: GitHub organization activity and Discord discussion. Not a family thing.
Vault: needs a reachable HashiCorp Vault server; overkill for a handful of keys.

1Password: the plugin needs a service account and the op CLI on the host; the browser sign-in flow needs a person at the Mac plus Claude Code with Chrome; and the bundled 1password skill lets an agent read secrets, which must never be on a family agent.
AUT-16.safety: Each item would add a public endpoint, a second trust domain, a coding harness with host access, or a secret-reading tool. All are ruled out by the roadmap; these are not features to harden, they are features to leave uninstalled.
unverified: 1Password service-account plan requirements and pricing (the vendor page redirected and was not fetched).
